## Building an Author API Step by Step

Click through each tab to see how a model, service, controller, and Litestar app fit together:

```python
class AuthorModel(base.UUIDBase):
    """Author database model."""

    __tablename__ = "litestar_basic_author"
    name: Mapped[str]

class AuthorCreate(msgspec.Struct):
    """Payload for creating an author."""

    name: str

class AuthorSchema(msgspec.Struct):
    """Serialized author schema."""

    id: UUID
    name: str

AuthorDTO = SQLAlchemyDTO[AuthorModel]
AuthorWriteDTO = SQLAlchemyDTO[
    Annotated[
        AuthorModel,
        SQLAlchemyDTOConfig(exclude={"id"}),
    ]
]
```

```python
class AuthorRepository(repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository[AuthorModel]):
    """Author async repository."""

    model_type = AuthorModel

class AuthorService(service.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepositoryService[AuthorModel, AuthorRepository]):
    """Author async repository service."""

    repository_type = AuthorRepository
```

```python
class AuthorController(Controller):
    """Author HTTP endpoints."""

    path = "/authors"
    dependencies = providers.create_service_dependencies(
        AuthorService,
        "authors_service",
        filters={"id_filter": UUID, "search": "name", "pagination_type": "limit_offset"},
    )

    @post(path="/")
    async def create_author(
        self,
        authors_service: NamedDependency[AuthorService],
        data: AuthorCreate,
    ) -> AuthorSchema:
        """Create a new author record."""
        obj = await authors_service.create(data, auto_commit=True)
        return authors_service.to_schema(obj, schema_type=AuthorSchema)

    @get(path="/")
    async def list_authors(
        self,
        authors_service: NamedDependency[AuthorService],
        filters: NamedDependency[SkipValidation[list[filters.FilterTypes]]],
    ) -> service.OffsetPagination[AuthorSchema]:
        """List authors with standard pagination and filtering."""
        results, total = await authors_service.get_many_and_count(*filters)
        return authors_service.to_schema(
            results,
            total,
            filters=filters,
            schema_type=AuthorSchema,
        )
```

```python
def create_app() -> Litestar:
    """Construct the Litestar application with an in-memory SQLite database."""
    return Litestar(
        route_handlers=[AuthorController],
        plugins=[
            SQLAlchemyPlugin(
                config=SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(
                    connection_string="sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:",
                    create_all=True,
                ),
            ),
        ],
    )
```

## Auto-Generating DTOs from Models

Don’t want to write separate `msgspec` or Pydantic schemas for simple CRUD endpoints? `SQLAlchemyDTO` inspects your model’s columns, relationships, and read-only `@property` fields automatically:

```python
from functools import cached_property
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar import SQLAlchemyDTO, base

class UserAccount(base.UUIDAuditBase):
    __tablename__ = "litestar_doc_user_account"
    first_name: Mapped[str]
    last_name: Mapped[str]

    @property
    def full_name(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.first_name} {self.last_name}"

    @cached_property
    def display_length(self) -> int:
        return len(self.full_name)

UserAccountDTO = SQLAlchemyDTO[UserAccount]
```

## Complete Runnable App

```python
"""Basic Litestar application with Advanced Alchemy service, DTO, and controller integration."""

from http import HTTPStatus
from typing import Annotated
from uuid import UUID

import msgspec
from litestar import Controller, Litestar, get, post
from litestar.di import NamedDependency
from litestar.params import SkipValidation
from litestar.testing import TestClient
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped

from advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar import (
    SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig,
    SQLAlchemyDTO,
    SQLAlchemyDTOConfig,
    SQLAlchemyPlugin,
    base,
    filters,
    providers,
    repository,
    service,
)

__all__ = (
    "AuthorController",
    "AuthorCreate",
    "AuthorDTO",
    "AuthorModel",
    "AuthorRepository",
    "AuthorSchema",
    "AuthorService",
    "AuthorWriteDTO",
    "create_app",
    "main",
)

class AuthorModel(base.UUIDBase):
    """Author database model."""

    __tablename__ = "litestar_basic_author"
    name: Mapped[str]

class AuthorCreate(msgspec.Struct):
    """Payload for creating an author."""

    name: str

class AuthorSchema(msgspec.Struct):
    """Serialized author schema."""

    id: UUID
    name: str

AuthorDTO = SQLAlchemyDTO[AuthorModel]
AuthorWriteDTO = SQLAlchemyDTO[
    Annotated[
        AuthorModel,
        SQLAlchemyDTOConfig(exclude={"id"}),
    ]
]

class AuthorRepository(repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository[AuthorModel]):
    """Author async repository."""

    model_type = AuthorModel

class AuthorService(service.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepositoryService[AuthorModel, AuthorRepository]):
    """Author async repository service."""

    repository_type = AuthorRepository

class AuthorController(Controller):
    """Author HTTP endpoints."""

    path = "/authors"
    dependencies = providers.create_service_dependencies(
        AuthorService,
        "authors_service",
        filters={"id_filter": UUID, "search": "name", "pagination_type": "limit_offset"},
    )

    @post(path="/")
    async def create_author(
        self,
        authors_service: NamedDependency[AuthorService],
        data: AuthorCreate,
    ) -> AuthorSchema:
        """Create a new author record."""
        obj = await authors_service.create(data, auto_commit=True)
        return authors_service.to_schema(obj, schema_type=AuthorSchema)

    @get(path="/")
    async def list_authors(
        self,
        authors_service: NamedDependency[AuthorService],
        filters: NamedDependency[SkipValidation[list[filters.FilterTypes]]],
    ) -> service.OffsetPagination[AuthorSchema]:
        """List authors with standard pagination and filtering."""
        results, total = await authors_service.get_many_and_count(*filters)
        return authors_service.to_schema(
            results,
            total,
            filters=filters,
            schema_type=AuthorSchema,
        )

def create_app() -> Litestar:
    """Construct the Litestar application with an in-memory SQLite database."""
    return Litestar(
        route_handlers=[AuthorController],
        plugins=[
            SQLAlchemyPlugin(
                config=SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(
                    connection_string="sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:",
                    create_all=True,
                ),
            ),
        ],
    )

def main() -> None:
    """Execute the basic Litestar application example in-process."""
    app = create_app()
    with TestClient(app=app) as client:
        create_response = client.post("/authors/", json={"name": "Ada Lovelace"})
        if create_response.status_code != HTTPStatus.CREATED:
            msg = f"Unexpected create status: {create_response.status_code}"
            raise RuntimeError(msg)
        created = create_response.json()
        if created["name"] != "Ada Lovelace":
            msg = f"Unexpected created author name: {created['name']}"
            raise RuntimeError(msg)

        list_response = client.get("/authors/?currentPage=1&pageSize=10")
        if list_response.status_code != HTTPStatus.OK:
            msg = f"Unexpected list status: {list_response.status_code}"
            raise RuntimeError(msg)
        payload = list_response.json()
        if payload["total"] != 1 or payload["items"][0]["name"] != "Ada Lovelace":
            msg = f"Unexpected list payload: {payload}"
            raise RuntimeError(msg)
```

# Litestar Services, Filters and DTOs

When building CRUD routes in Litestar, you rarely want to wire up `db_session` manually or hand-write query parameters for pagination, search, and sorting on every controller.

Advanced Alchemy provides two Litestar helpers that remove that boilerplate:

1. **Service & Filter Dependencies** (`create_service_dependencies`) — injects your service and pre-built query filters directly into controller methods.
2. **SQLAlchemy DTOs** (`SQLAlchemyDTO`) — generates Litestar request and response DTOs straight from your SQLAlchemy models.

## Injecting Services and Query Filters

Declare `dependencies = create_service_dependencies(...)` on a Litestar `Controller` to inject both your service and a `filters: list[FilterTypes]` parameter with automatic OpenAPI query parameters:

```python
from typing import Annotated
from uuid import UUID
from litestar import Controller, get
from litestar.params import Dependency
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar import base, filters, providers, repository, service

class ProductModel(base.UUIDAuditBase):
    __tablename__ = "litestar_dto_product"
    name: Mapped[str]

class ProductRepository(repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository[ProductModel]):
    model_type = ProductModel

class ProductService(service.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepositoryService[ProductModel, ProductRepository]):
    repository_type = ProductRepository

class ProductController(Controller):
    path = "/products"
    dependencies = providers.create_service_dependencies(
        ProductService,
        key="products_service",
        filters=providers.FilterConfig(
            id_filter=UUID,
            search="name",
            pagination_type="limit_offset",
            pagination_size=20,
            created_at=True,
            updated_at=True,
        ),
    )

    @get("/")
    async def list_products(
        self,
        products_service: ProductService,
        filters: Annotated[list[filters.FilterTypes], Dependency(skip_validation=True)],
    ) -> list[ProductModel]:
        results, _ = await products_service.get_many_and_count(*filters)
        return list(results)
```

If a route only needs the service without query filters, use `create_service_provider(ProductService)` instead.

## Auto-Generating DTOs from Models

Instead of maintaining separate schema classes for simple tables, `SQLAlchemyDTO` inspects your SQLAlchemy columns, relationships, `@property`, and `@cached_property` attributes automatically:

```python
from functools import cached_property
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar import SQLAlchemyDTO, SQLAlchemyDTOConfig, base

class UserAccount(base.UUIDAuditBase):
    __tablename__ = "litestar_dto_user_account"
    first_name: Mapped[str]
    last_name: Mapped[str]
    password_hash: Mapped[str]

    @property
    def full_name(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.first_name} {self.last_name}"

    @cached_property
    def initials(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.first_name[:1]}{self.last_name[:1]}".upper()

class UserReadDTO(SQLAlchemyDTO[UserAccount]):
    config = SQLAlchemyDTOConfig(
        exclude={"password_hash"},
        rename_strategy="camel",
    )
```

```python
class UserCreateDTO(SQLAlchemyDTO[UserAccount]):
    config = SQLAlchemyDTOConfig(
        exclude={"id", "created_at", "updated_at", "full_name", "initials"},
    )

class UserPatchDTO(SQLAlchemyDTO[UserAccount]):
    config = SQLAlchemyDTOConfig(
        exclude={"id", "created_at", "updated_at", "full_name", "initials"},
        partial=True,
    )
```

Source: https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/usage/frameworks/litestar_sessions.html

# Litestar Database and Server Sessions

This guide covers two kinds of “sessions” in Litestar:

1. **Database sessions**: The SQLAlchemy connection used by your routes to read and save rows during a request.
2. **Server-side user sessions**: Keeping logged-in user state (like shopping carts or auth data) inside a database table instead of Redis.

## Per-Request Database Sessions

When `SQLAlchemyPlugin` is registered, Litestar injects a database session under the `db_session` parameter name. You can control when changes commit by setting `before_send_handler` on your config:

- `"autocommit"` saves changes automatically when a route returns a normal `2xx` response and rolls back on errors.
- `"autocommit_include_redirects"` also commits when a route returns a `3xx` redirect (useful for HTML form submissions).

Need a session outside a web request, such as in a startup hook or background script? Open one directly with `async with config.get_session() as db_session:`.

## Connecting Multiple Databases

To talk to both a main database and an analytics database in one Litestar app, pass a list of configs with unique `session_dependency_key`, `engine_dependency_key`, and `bind_key` names:

```python
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar import SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig, SQLAlchemyPlugin

primary_config = SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(
    connection_string="sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:",
    session_dependency_key="primary_session",
    engine_dependency_key="primary_engine",
    bind_key="primary",
)
analytics_config = SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(
    connection_string="sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:",
    session_dependency_key="analytics_session",
    engine_dependency_key="analytics_engine",
    bind_key="analytics",
)
plugin = SQLAlchemyPlugin(config=[primary_config, analytics_config])
```

## Storing User Sessions in Your Database

Instead of running a separate Redis server just for user login cookies or rate-limit counters, you can store them in your SQL database using `SQLAlchemyStore` or `SQLAlchemyAsyncSessionBackend`:

```python
class AppStoreModel(StoreModelMixin):
    """Database table backing Litestar's server-side session store."""

    __tablename__ = "litestar_app_store"
```

```python
@post(path="/session/{key:str}/{value:str}")
async def set_session_value(
    key: FromPath[str],
    value: FromPath[str],
    request: Request[Any, Any, Any],
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Store a key-value pair in the server-side session."""
    request.session[key] = value
    return {"key": key, "value": value}

@get(path="/session/{key:str}")
async def get_session_value(
    key: FromPath[str],
    request: Request[Any, Any, Any],
) -> dict[str, Optional[str]]:
    """Read a key-value pair from the server-side session."""
    return {"key": key, "value": request.session.get(key)}
```

```python
def create_app(db_path: Path, storage_dir: Path) -> Litestar:
    """Create a Litestar application configured with SQLAlchemyStore and StoredObject."""
    storages.register_backend(f"file://{storage_dir}", key="litestar_docs_fs")
    alchemy_config = SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(
        connection_string=f"sqlite+aiosqlite:///{db_path}",
        create_all=True,
    )
    session_store = SQLAlchemyStore(config=alchemy_config, model=AppStoreModel)
    session_config = ServerSideSessionConfig(store="sessions")

    return Litestar(
        route_handlers=[set_session_value, get_session_value, upload_attachment],
        plugins=[SQLAlchemyPlugin(config=alchemy_config)],
        middleware=[session_config.middleware],
        stores=StoreRegistry(stores={"sessions": session_store}),
    )
```

```python
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.session import (
    SQLAlchemyAsyncSessionBackend,
    SessionModelMixin,
)

class UserSessionModel(SessionModelMixin):
    __tablename__ = "litestar_user_sessions"

assert issubclass(UserSessionModel, SessionModelMixin)
assert SQLAlchemyAsyncSessionBackend is not None
```

Both approaches use native database upserts and include a `delete_expired()` helper to clear old session rows on a schedule.

Source: https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/usage/frameworks/litestar_storage.html

# Litestar File and Object Storage

Uploading user avatars, invoices, or attachments usually creates headaches: if a database commit fails after uploading to S3, you get orphaned files; if a row is deleted, someone forgets to delete the file in storage.

`StoredObject` and `FileObject` keep your files and database rows in lockstep—uploading files when your transaction commits and deleting old files automatically when rows are removed or replaced.

## Uploading Files in Three Steps

```python
class AttachmentModel(base.UUIDBase):
    """Document attachment model with StoredObject metadata."""

    __tablename__ = "litestar_attachment"
    title: Mapped[str]
    document: Mapped[Optional[FileObject]] = mapped_column(
        StoredObject(backend="litestar_docs_fs"),
        nullable=True,
    )

class AttachmentSchema(msgspec.Struct):
    """Serialized attachment response payload."""

    id: UUID
    title: str
    filename: Optional[str] = None
```

```python
@post(
    path="/attachments",
    dependencies=providers.create_service_dependencies(AttachmentService, "attachments_service"),
)
async def upload_attachment(
    data: dict[str, str],
    attachments_service: NamedDependency[AttachmentService],
) -> AttachmentSchema:
    """Persist an attachment record and its StoredObject file payload."""
    file_obj = FileObject(
        backend="litestar_docs_fs",
        filename=data["filename"],
        content_type="text/plain",
        content=data["content"].encode("utf-8"),
    )
    record = await attachments_service.create(
        {"title": data["title"], "document": file_obj},
        auto_commit=True,
    )
    return AttachmentSchema(
        id=record.id,
        title=record.title,
        filename=record.document.filename if record.document else None,
    )
```

```python
def create_app(db_path: Path, storage_dir: Path) -> Litestar:
    """Create a Litestar application configured with SQLAlchemyStore and StoredObject."""
    storages.register_backend(f"file://{storage_dir}", key="litestar_docs_fs")
    alchemy_config = SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(
        connection_string=f"sqlite+aiosqlite:///{db_path}",
        create_all=True,
    )
    session_store = SQLAlchemyStore(config=alchemy_config, model=AppStoreModel)
    session_config = ServerSideSessionConfig(store="sessions")

    return Litestar(
        route_handlers=[set_session_value, get_session_value, upload_attachment],
        plugins=[SQLAlchemyPlugin(config=alchemy_config)],
        middleware=[session_config.middleware],
        stores=StoreRegistry(stores={"sessions": session_store}),
    )
```

## Custom JSON Encoders

If your database driver needs custom JSON helpers for file metadata, pass `json_serializer` and `json_deserializer` on `EngineConfig`:

```python
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar import EngineConfig, SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig
from advanced_alchemy.utils.serialization import decode_json, encode_json

alchemy_config = SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(
    connection_string="sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:",
    engine_config=EngineConfig(
        json_serializer=encode_json,
        json_deserializer=decode_json,
    ),
)
```

## Complete Runnable Example

```python
"""Litestar server-side session store and StoredObject file storage example."""

import tempfile
from http import HTTPStatus
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Optional
from uuid import UUID

import msgspec
from litestar import Litestar, Request, get, post
from litestar.di import NamedDependency
from litestar.middleware.session.server_side import ServerSideSessionConfig
from litestar.params import FromPath
from litestar.stores.registry import StoreRegistry
from litestar.testing import TestClient
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar import (
    SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig,
    SQLAlchemyPlugin,
    base,
    providers,
    repository,
    service,
)
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.store import SQLAlchemyStore, StoreModelMixin
from advanced_alchemy.types import FileObject, StoredObject, storages

__all__ = (
    "AppStoreModel",
    "AttachmentModel",
    "AttachmentRepository",
    "AttachmentSchema",
    "AttachmentService",
    "create_app",
    "main",
)

class AppStoreModel(StoreModelMixin):
    """Database table backing Litestar's server-side session store."""

    __tablename__ = "litestar_app_store"

class AttachmentModel(base.UUIDBase):
    """Document attachment model with StoredObject metadata."""

    __tablename__ = "litestar_attachment"
    title: Mapped[str]
    document: Mapped[Optional[FileObject]] = mapped_column(
        StoredObject(backend="litestar_docs_fs"),
        nullable=True,
    )

class AttachmentSchema(msgspec.Struct):
    """Serialized attachment response payload."""

    id: UUID
    title: str
    filename: Optional[str] = None

class AttachmentRepository(repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository[AttachmentModel]):
    """Attachment async repository."""

    model_type = AttachmentModel

class AttachmentService(service.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepositoryService[AttachmentModel, AttachmentRepository]):
    """Attachment async service."""

    repository_type = AttachmentRepository

@post(path="/session/{key:str}/{value:str}")
async def set_session_value(
    key: FromPath[str],
    value: FromPath[str],
    request: Request[Any, Any, Any],
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Store a key-value pair in the server-side session."""
    request.session[key] = value
    return {"key": key, "value": value}

@get(path="/session/{key:str}")
async def get_session_value(
    key: FromPath[str],
    request: Request[Any, Any, Any],
) -> dict[str, Optional[str]]:
    """Read a key-value pair from the server-side session."""
    return {"key": key, "value": request.session.get(key)}

@post(
    path="/attachments",
    dependencies=providers.create_service_dependencies(AttachmentService, "attachments_service"),
)
async def upload_attachment(
    data: dict[str, str],
    attachments_service: NamedDependency[AttachmentService],
) -> AttachmentSchema:
    """Persist an attachment record and its StoredObject file payload."""
    file_obj = FileObject(
        backend="litestar_docs_fs",
        filename=data["filename"],
        content_type="text/plain",
        content=data["content"].encode("utf-8"),
    )
    record = await attachments_service.create(
        {"title": data["title"], "document": file_obj},
        auto_commit=True,
    )
    return AttachmentSchema(
        id=record.id,
        title=record.title,
        filename=record.document.filename if record.document else None,
    )

def create_app(db_path: Path, storage_dir: Path) -> Litestar:
    """Create a Litestar application configured with SQLAlchemyStore and StoredObject."""
    storages.register_backend(f"file://{storage_dir}", key="litestar_docs_fs")
    alchemy_config = SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(
        connection_string=f"sqlite+aiosqlite:///{db_path}",
        create_all=True,
    )
    session_store = SQLAlchemyStore(config=alchemy_config, model=AppStoreModel)
    session_config = ServerSideSessionConfig(store="sessions")

    return Litestar(
        route_handlers=[set_session_value, get_session_value, upload_attachment],
        plugins=[SQLAlchemyPlugin(config=alchemy_config)],
        middleware=[session_config.middleware],
        stores=StoreRegistry(stores={"sessions": session_store}),
    )

def main() -> None:
    """Execute the session store and StoredObject Litestar example inside a temporary directory."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp_dir:
        base_dir = Path(tmp_dir)
        db_file = base_dir / "session_store.sqlite"
        storage_dir = base_dir / "uploads"
        storage_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        app = create_app(db_file, storage_dir)
        with TestClient(app=app) as client:
            set_res = client.post("/session/theme/dark")
            if set_res.status_code != HTTPStatus.CREATED:
                msg = f"Unexpected session set status: {set_res.status_code}"
                raise RuntimeError(msg)

            get_res = client.get("/session/theme")
            if get_res.status_code != HTTPStatus.OK or get_res.json() != {"key": "theme", "value": "dark"}:
                msg = f"Unexpected session get response: {get_res.status_code} {get_res.text}"
                raise RuntimeError(msg)

            upload_res = client.post(
                "/attachments",
                json={"title": "Architecture Spec", "filename": "spec.txt", "content": "Stored via Advanced Alchemy"},
            )
            if upload_res.status_code != HTTPStatus.CREATED:
                msg = f"Unexpected upload status: {upload_res.status_code}"
                raise RuntimeError(msg)
            payload = upload_res.json()
            if payload["title"] != "Architecture Spec" or payload["filename"] != "spec.txt":
                msg = f"Unexpected upload payload: {payload}"
                raise RuntimeError(msg)
        storages.clear_backends()
```

```python
"""Litestar server-side session store and StoredObject file storage example."""

import tempfile
from http import HTTPStatus
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any
from uuid import UUID

import msgspec
from litestar import Litestar, Request, get, post
from litestar.di import NamedDependency
from litestar.middleware.session.server_side import ServerSideSessionConfig
from litestar.params import FromPath
from litestar.stores.registry import StoreRegistry
from litestar.testing import TestClient
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar import (
    SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig,
    SQLAlchemyPlugin,
    base,
    providers,
    repository,
    service,
)
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.store import SQLAlchemyStore, StoreModelMixin
from advanced_alchemy.types import FileObject, StoredObject, storages

__all__ = (
    "AppStoreModel",
    "AttachmentModel",
    "AttachmentRepository",
    "AttachmentSchema",
    "AttachmentService",
    "create_app",
    "main",
)

class AppStoreModel(StoreModelMixin):
    """Database table backing Litestar's server-side session store."""

    __tablename__ = "litestar_app_store"

class AttachmentModel(base.UUIDBase):
    """Document attachment model with StoredObject metadata."""

    __tablename__ = "litestar_attachment"
    title: Mapped[str]
    document: Mapped[FileObject | None] = mapped_column(
        StoredObject(backend="litestar_docs_fs"),
        nullable=True,
    )

class AttachmentSchema(msgspec.Struct):
    """Serialized attachment response payload."""

    id: UUID
    title: str
    filename: str | None = None

class AttachmentRepository(repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository[AttachmentModel]):
    """Attachment async repository."""

    model_type = AttachmentModel

class AttachmentService(service.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepositoryService[AttachmentModel, AttachmentRepository]):
    """Attachment async service."""

    repository_type = AttachmentRepository

@post(path="/session/{key:str}/{value:str}")
async def set_session_value(
    key: FromPath[str],
    value: FromPath[str],
    request: Request[Any, Any, Any],
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Store a key-value pair in the server-side session."""
    request.session[key] = value
    return {"key": key, "value": value}

@get(path="/session/{key:str}")
async def get_session_value(
    key: FromPath[str],
    request: Request[Any, Any, Any],
) -> dict[str, str | None]:
    """Read a key-value pair from the server-side session."""
    return {"key": key, "value": request.session.get(key)}

@post(
    path="/attachments",
    dependencies=providers.create_service_dependencies(AttachmentService, "attachments_service"),
)
async def upload_attachment(
    data: dict[str, str],
    attachments_service: NamedDependency[AttachmentService],
) -> AttachmentSchema:
    """Persist an attachment record and its StoredObject file payload."""
    file_obj = FileObject(
        backend="litestar_docs_fs",
        filename=data["filename"],
        content_type="text/plain",
        content=data["content"].encode("utf-8"),
    )
    record = await attachments_service.create(
        {"title": data["title"], "document": file_obj},
        auto_commit=True,
    )
    return AttachmentSchema(
        id=record.id,
        title=record.title,
        filename=record.document.filename if record.document else None,
    )

def create_app(db_path: Path, storage_dir: Path) -> Litestar:
    """Create a Litestar application configured with SQLAlchemyStore and StoredObject."""
    storages.register_backend(f"file://{storage_dir}", key="litestar_docs_fs")
    alchemy_config = SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(
        connection_string=f"sqlite+aiosqlite:///{db_path}",
        create_all=True,
    )
    session_store = SQLAlchemyStore(config=alchemy_config, model=AppStoreModel)
    session_config = ServerSideSessionConfig(store="sessions")

    return Litestar(
        route_handlers=[set_session_value, get_session_value, upload_attachment],
        plugins=[SQLAlchemyPlugin(config=alchemy_config)],
        middleware=[session_config.middleware],
        stores=StoreRegistry(stores={"sessions": session_store}),
    )

def main() -> None:
    """Execute the session store and StoredObject Litestar example inside a temporary directory."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp_dir:
        base_dir = Path(tmp_dir)
        db_file = base_dir / "session_store.sqlite"
        storage_dir = base_dir / "uploads"
        storage_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        app = create_app(db_file, storage_dir)
        with TestClient(app=app) as client:
            set_res = client.post("/session/theme/dark")
            if set_res.status_code != HTTPStatus.CREATED:
                msg = f"Unexpected session set status: {set_res.status_code}"
                raise RuntimeError(msg)

            get_res = client.get("/session/theme")
            if get_res.status_code != HTTPStatus.OK or get_res.json() != {"key": "theme", "value": "dark"}:
                msg = f"Unexpected session get response: {get_res.status_code} {get_res.text}"
                raise RuntimeError(msg)

            upload_res = client.post(
                "/attachments",
                json={"title": "Architecture Spec", "filename": "spec.txt", "content": "Stored via Advanced Alchemy"},
            )
            if upload_res.status_code != HTTPStatus.CREATED:
                msg = f"Unexpected upload status: {upload_res.status_code}"
                raise RuntimeError(msg)
            payload = upload_res.json()
            if payload["title"] != "Architecture Spec" or payload["filename"] != "spec.txt":
                msg = f"Unexpected upload payload: {payload}"
                raise RuntimeError(msg)
        storages.clear_backends()
```

# FastAPI Integration

Advanced Alchemy plugs into FastAPI through the `AdvancedAlchemy` extension, managing database startup/shutdown automatically and giving your routes clean `Depends(...)` helpers for sessions, services, and OpenAPI-documented search/pagination filters.

## What’s Included for FastAPI

| Feature | What It Gives You | Guide & API |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Lifespan & Sessions** | Starts and disposes engines automatically and opens a fresh database session per request. | [API](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/fastapi/index.html) |
| **Depends Helpers** | `provide_session`, `provide_service`, and `provide_filters` (with automatic Swagger UI query params). | [Guide](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/usage/frameworks/fastapi_dependencies.html) · [API](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/fastapi/index.html) |
| **Uploads & Multi-Binds** | Multipart `UploadFile` storage columns and support for multiple databases in one app. | [Guide](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/usage/frameworks/fastapi_storage.html) · [API](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/types.html) |
| **Migrations CLI** | Works directly with the `alchemy` CLI to generate and run Alembic migrations. | [CLI Guide](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/usage/cli.html) |

## Installation

```bash
uv add advanced-alchemy fastapi aiosqlite
```

```bash
pip install advanced-alchemy fastapi aiosqlite
```

```bash

```

## Building a FastAPI Service Step by Step

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.fastapi import (
    AdvancedAlchemy,
    AsyncSessionConfig,
    SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig,
)

app = FastAPI()
alchemy = AdvancedAlchemy(
    config=SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(
        connection_string="sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:",
        session_config=AsyncSessionConfig(expire_on_commit=False),
        create_all=True,
        commit_mode="autocommit",
    ),
    app=app,
)
```

```python
class AuthorModel(base.UUIDBase):
    """Author database model for FastAPI example."""

    __tablename__ = "fastapi_basic_author"
    name: Mapped[str]

class AuthorCreate(BaseModel):
    """Request payload for creating an author."""

    name: str

class AuthorSchema(BaseModel):
    """Response schema for an author record."""

    model_config = {"from_attributes": True}

    id: UUID
    name: str

class AuthorRepository(repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository[AuthorModel]):
    """Author async repository."""

    model_type = AuthorModel

class AuthorService(service.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepositoryService[AuthorModel, AuthorRepository]):
    """Author async repository service."""

    repository_type = AuthorRepository
```

```python
def create_app(db_path: Path) -> FastAPI:
    """Create a FastAPI application wired with AdvancedAlchemy service and filter providers."""
    app = FastAPI()
    alchemy_config = SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(
        connection_string=f"sqlite+aiosqlite:///{db_path}",
        session_config=AsyncSessionConfig(expire_on_commit=False),
        create_all=True,
        commit_mode="autocommit",
    )
    alchemy = AdvancedAlchemy(config=alchemy_config, app=app)
    router = APIRouter()

    @router.post("/authors", status_code=int(HTTPStatus.CREATED))
    async def create_author(
        data: AuthorCreate,
        authors_service: Annotated[AuthorService, Depends(alchemy.provide_service(AuthorService))],
    ) -> AuthorSchema:
        """Create a new author record."""
        obj = await authors_service.create(data)
        return authors_service.to_schema(obj, schema_type=AuthorSchema)

    @router.get("/authors")
    async def list_authors(
        authors_service: Annotated[AuthorService, Depends(alchemy.provide_service(AuthorService))],
        filters: Annotated[
            list[filters.FilterTypes],
            Depends(
                alchemy.provide_filters(
                    {
                        "id_filter": UUID,
                        "search": "name",
                        "pagination_type": "limit_offset",
                    },
                ),
            ),
        ],
    ) -> service.OffsetPagination[AuthorSchema]:
        """List authors with limit/offset pagination and search filters."""
        results, total = await authors_service.get_many_and_count(*filters)
        return authors_service.to_schema(
            results,
            total,
            filters=filters,
            schema_type=AuthorSchema,
        )

    app.include_router(router)
    return app
```

> **Tip**: Using multiple databases? Pass the bind key to `alchemy.provide_session("reporting")` or `alchemy.provide_service(ReportService, key="reporting")`.

## Complete Runnable App

```python
"""FastAPI service and filter dependency injection example with Advanced Alchemy."""

import tempfile
from http import HTTPStatus
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Annotated
from uuid import UUID

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, FastAPI
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from pydantic import BaseModel
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped

from advanced_alchemy.extensions.fastapi import (
    AdvancedAlchemy,
    AsyncSessionConfig,
    SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig,
    base,
    filters,
    repository,
    service,
)

__all__ = (
    "AuthorCreate",
    "AuthorModel",
    "AuthorRepository",
    "AuthorSchema",
    "AuthorService",
    "create_app",
    "main",
)

class AuthorModel(base.UUIDBase):
    """Author database model for FastAPI example."""

    __tablename__ = "fastapi_basic_author"
    name: Mapped[str]

class AuthorCreate(BaseModel):
    """Request payload for creating an author."""

    name: str

class AuthorSchema(BaseModel):
    """Response schema for an author record."""

    model_config = {"from_attributes": True}

    id: UUID
    name: str

class AuthorRepository(repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository[AuthorModel]):
    """Author async repository."""

    model_type = AuthorModel

class AuthorService(service.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepositoryService[AuthorModel, AuthorRepository]):
    """Author async repository service."""

    repository_type = AuthorRepository

def create_app(db_path: Path) -> FastAPI:
    """Create a FastAPI application wired with AdvancedAlchemy service and filter providers."""
    app = FastAPI()
    alchemy_config = SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(
        connection_string=f"sqlite+aiosqlite:///{db_path}",
        session_config=AsyncSessionConfig(expire_on_commit=False),
        create_all=True,
        commit_mode="autocommit",
    )
    alchemy = AdvancedAlchemy(config=alchemy_config, app=app)
    router = APIRouter()

    @router.post("/authors", status_code=int(HTTPStatus.CREATED))
    async def create_author(
        data: AuthorCreate,
        authors_service: Annotated[AuthorService, Depends(alchemy.provide_service(AuthorService))],
    ) -> AuthorSchema:
        """Create a new author record."""
        obj = await authors_service.create(data)
        return authors_service.to_schema(obj, schema_type=AuthorSchema)

    @router.get("/authors")
    async def list_authors(
        authors_service: Annotated[AuthorService, Depends(alchemy.provide_service(AuthorService))],
        filters: Annotated[
            list[filters.FilterTypes],
            Depends(
                alchemy.provide_filters(
                    {
                        "id_filter": UUID,
                        "search": "name",
                        "pagination_type": "limit_offset",
                    },
                ),
            ),
        ],
    ) -> service.OffsetPagination[AuthorSchema]:
        """List authors with limit/offset pagination and search filters."""
        results, total = await authors_service.get_many_and_count(*filters)
        return authors_service.to_schema(
            results,
            total,
            filters=filters,
            schema_type=AuthorSchema,
        )

    app.include_router(router)
    return app

def main() -> None:
    """Execute the FastAPI dependency injection example in-process."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp_dir:
        db_file = Path(tmp_dir) / "fastapi_example.sqlite"
        app = create_app(db_file)
        with TestClient(app=app) as client:
            create_res = client.post("/authors", json={"name": "Grace Hopper"})
            if create_res.status_code != HTTPStatus.CREATED:
                msg = f"Unexpected create status: {create_res.status_code}"
                raise RuntimeError(msg)
            created = create_res.json()
            if created["name"] != "Grace Hopper":
                msg = f"Unexpected created author name: {created['name']}"
                raise RuntimeError(msg)

            list_res = client.get("/authors?currentPage=1&pageSize=10")
            if list_res.status_code != HTTPStatus.OK:
                msg = f"Unexpected list status: {list_res.status_code}"
                raise RuntimeError(msg)
            payload = list_res.json()
            if payload["total"] != 1 or payload["items"][0]["name"] != "Grace Hopper":
                msg = f"Unexpected list payload: {payload}"
                raise RuntimeError(msg)
```

# FastAPI Services and Filter Depends

FastAPI routes use `Depends(...)` to inject database sessions, services, and query parameters. Advanced Alchemy’s `AdvancedAlchemy` extension builds these `Depends` callables for you and adds pagination, search, sorting, and date-range parameters straight into FastAPI’s Swagger UI.

## Injecting Sessions and Services

Use `alchemy.provide_session()` when a route needs a raw SQLAlchemy session, or `alchemy.provide_service(ServiceClass)` when you want a ready-to-use service:

```python
from typing import Annotated
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.fastapi import (
    AdvancedAlchemy,
    AsyncSessionConfig,
    SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig,
    base,
    repository,
    service,
)

class AuthorModel(base.UUIDBase):
    __tablename__ = "fastapi_dep_author"
    name: Mapped[str]

class AuthorRepository(repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository[AuthorModel]):
    model_type = AuthorModel

class AuthorService(service.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepositoryService[AuthorModel, AuthorRepository]):
    repository_type = AuthorRepository

app = FastAPI()
alchemy = AdvancedAlchemy(
    config=SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(
        connection_string="sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:",
        session_config=AsyncSessionConfig(expire_on_commit=False),
        commit_mode="autocommit",
        create_all=True,
    ),
    app=app,
)

AuthorsServiceDep = Annotated[AuthorService, Depends(alchemy.provide_service(AuthorService))]
```

```python
from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

async def provide_custom_authors(
    db_session: Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(alchemy.provide_session())],
) -> AsyncGenerator[AuthorService, None]:
    async with AuthorService.new(session=db_session) as authors_service:
        yield authors_service
```

```python
from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

async def provide_custom_authors(
    db_session: Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(alchemy.provide_session())],
) -> AsyncGenerator[AuthorService]:
    async with AuthorService.new(session=db_session) as authors_service:
        yield authors_service
```

## Adding Search and Pagination to Swagger UI

Pass a `FilterConfig` dictionary to `alchemy.provide_filters(...)` to generate FastAPI `Depends` parameters for pagination, text search, sorting, and date filters:

```python
from uuid import UUID
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.fastapi import filters

AuthorFiltersDep = Annotated[
    list[filters.FilterTypes],
    Depends(
        alchemy.provide_filters(
            {
                "id_filter": UUID,
                "search": "name",
                "search_ignore_case": True,
                "pagination_type": "limit_offset",
                "pagination_size": 20,
                "sort_field": "name",
                "created_at": True,
            }
        )
    ),
]

@app.get("/authors")
async def list_authors(
    authors_service: AuthorsServiceDep,
    filters: AuthorFiltersDep,
) -> dict[str, int]:
    _, total = await authors_service.get_many_and_count(*filters)
    return {"total": total}
```

# FastAPI File Storage and Multi-Binds

This guide shows how to attach uploaded files to SQLAlchemy models in FastAPI and how to connect a single FastAPI app to more than one database.

## Storing Uploaded Files

Register a local folder or cloud bucket (S3, GCS, Azure) in `storages` and add a `StoredObject` column to your model. In FastAPI routes that receive an `UploadFile`, pass `FileObject(backend=..., filename=file.filename, content=await file.read())` to `service.create(...)`—Advanced Alchemy saves the file when the transaction commits and deletes it if the row is deleted:

```python
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
from typing import Optional
from uuid import UUID
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.fastapi import base, repository, service
from advanced_alchemy.types import FileObject, StoredObject, storages

storage_tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
storages.register_backend(f"file://{Path(storage_tmp)}", key="fastapi_documents")

class DocumentModel(base.UUIDBase):
    __tablename__ = "fastapi_document"

    name: Mapped[str]
    file: Mapped[Optional[FileObject]] = mapped_column(
        StoredObject(backend="fastapi_documents"),
        nullable=True,
    )

class DocumentRepository(repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository[DocumentModel]):
    model_type = DocumentModel

class DocumentService(service.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepositoryService[DocumentModel, DocumentRepository]):
    repository_type = DocumentRepository

class DocumentResponse(BaseModel):
    model_config = {"from_attributes": True}

    id: Optional[UUID] = None
    name: str
    file: Optional[FileObject] = Field(default=None, exclude=True)

storages.clear_backends()
```

```python
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
from uuid import UUID
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.fastapi import base, repository, service
from advanced_alchemy.types import FileObject, StoredObject, storages

storage_tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
storages.register_backend(f"file://{Path(storage_tmp)}", key="fastapi_documents")

class DocumentModel(base.UUIDBase):
    __tablename__ = "fastapi_document"

    name: Mapped[str]
    file: Mapped[FileObject | None] = mapped_column(
        StoredObject(backend="fastapi_documents"),
        nullable=True,
    )

class DocumentRepository(repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository[DocumentModel]):
    model_type = DocumentModel

class DocumentService(service.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepositoryService[DocumentModel, DocumentRepository]):
    repository_type = DocumentRepository

class DocumentResponse(BaseModel):
    model_config = {"from_attributes": True}

    id: UUID | None = None
    name: str
    file: FileObject | None = Field(default=None, exclude=True)

storages.clear_backends()
```

## Connecting Multiple Databases

Pass a list of configs with distinct `bind_key` names when your FastAPI app talks to more than one database (for example, an async main database and a sync reporting database):

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.fastapi import (
    AdvancedAlchemy,
    SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig,
    SQLAlchemySyncConfig,
)

app = FastAPI()
alchemy = AdvancedAlchemy(
    config=[
        SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(connection_string="sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:"),
        SQLAlchemySyncConfig(
            connection_string="sqlite+pysqlite:///:memory:",
            bind_key="reporting",
        ),
    ],
    app=app,
)
assert alchemy.get_async_config().bind_key == "default"
assert alchemy.get_sync_config("reporting").bind_key == "reporting"
```

Source: https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/usage/frameworks/starlette.html

# Starlette Integration

For lightweight ASGI services built on Starlette, `AdvancedAlchemy` manages engine startup/shutdown and attaches a request-scoped database session to `request.state` automatically.

## What’s Included for Starlette

| Feature | What It Gives You | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Session Middleware** | Opens and cleans up a SQLAlchemy session on `request.state` for every HTTP request. | [API](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/starlette/index.html) |
| **Commit Modes** | Supports manual commits, `"autocommit"` on `2xx`, and `"autocommit_include_redirect"`. | [API](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/starlette/index.html) |
| **Multi-Database Binds** | Connects multiple sync or async databases in a single Starlette app via `bind_key`. | [API](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/starlette/index.html) |

## Setup and Route Usage

Attach `AdvancedAlchemy` to your `Starlette` app and grab the current request’s session with `alchemy.get_async_session(request)`:

```python
from starlette.applications import Starlette
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.starlette import (
    AdvancedAlchemy,
    AsyncSessionConfig,
    SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig,
)

alchemy_config = SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(
    connection_string="sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:",
    session_config=AsyncSessionConfig(expire_on_commit=False),
    commit_mode="autocommit",
    create_all=True,
)

app = Starlette()
alchemy = AdvancedAlchemy(config=alchemy_config, app=app)
```

```python
from uuid import UUID
import msgspec
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped
from starlette.requests import Request
from starlette.responses import JSONResponse, Response
from starlette.routing import Route
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.starlette import base, filters, repository, service

class AuthorModel(base.UUIDBase):
    __tablename__ = "starlette_author"
    name: Mapped[str]

class AuthorSchema(msgspec.Struct):
    id: UUID
    name: str

class AuthorService(service.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepositoryService[AuthorModel]):
    class Repo(repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository[AuthorModel]):
        model_type = AuthorModel

    repository_type = Repo

async def list_authors(request: Request) -> Response:
    page = int(request.query_params.get("currentPage", 1))
    size = int(request.query_params.get("pageSize", 10))
    limit_offset = filters.LimitOffset(limit=size, offset=size * (page - 1))

    authors_service = AuthorService(session=alchemy.get_async_session(request))
    results, total = await authors_service.get_many_and_count(limit_offset)
    payload = authors_service.to_schema(
        results,
        total,
        filters=[limit_offset],
        schema_type=AuthorSchema,
    )
    return Response(content=msgspec.json.encode(payload), media_type="application/json")

async def healthcheck(request: Request) -> JSONResponse:
    db_session = alchemy.get_async_session(request)
    assert db_session is not None
    return JSONResponse({"dialect": alchemy.get_async_engine().dialect.name, "status": "ok"})

app.router.routes.extend(
    [
        Route("/authors", endpoint=list_authors, methods=["GET"]),
        Route("/health", endpoint=healthcheck, methods=["GET"]),
    ],
)
```

## Commit Modes and Multiple Databases

```python
redirect_config = SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(
    connection_string="sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:",
    commit_mode="autocommit_include_redirect",
)
redirect_app = Starlette()
redirect_alchemy = AdvancedAlchemy(config=redirect_config, app=redirect_app)
```

```python
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.starlette import SQLAlchemySyncConfig

multi_db_app = Starlette()
multi_alchemy = AdvancedAlchemy(
    config=[
        SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(connection_string="sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:"),
        SQLAlchemySyncConfig(connection_string="sqlite+pysqlite:///:memory:", bind_key="reporting"),
    ],
    app=multi_db_app,
)
assert multi_alchemy.get_async_config().bind_key == "default"
assert multi_alchemy.get_sync_config("reporting").bind_key == "reporting"
```

See [Starlette](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/starlette/index.html) for full API signatures.

Source: https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/usage/frameworks/flask.html

# Flask Integration

Advanced Alchemy plugs into both classic synchronous Flask apps and `async def` Flask routes—giving every request a managed SQLAlchemy session, adding a `jsonify()` helper onto your services, and registering `flask database` migration commands automatically.

## What’s Included for Flask

| Feature | What It Gives You | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **App-Context Sessions** | Reuses one session per Flask request and closes or commits it cleanly on teardown. | [API](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/flask/index.html) |
| **FlaskServiceMixin** | Adds `service.jsonify(...)` to return paginated `msgspec` or Pydantic schemas directly from routes. | [API](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/flask/index.html) |
| **Sync & Async Support** | Works with standard sync engines, async engines, and multiple databases via `bind_key`. | [API](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/flask/index.html) |
| **Flask CLI** | Registers `flask database init`, `upgrade`, and `downgrade` commands automatically. | [CLI Guide](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/usage/cli.html) |

## Sync, Async, and Multi-Database Setup

```python
from flask import Flask
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.flask import AdvancedAlchemy, SQLAlchemySyncConfig, base

class User(base.BigIntBase):
    __tablename__ = "flask_user_account"
    name: Mapped[str]

app = Flask("flask_basic_db")
alchemy = AdvancedAlchemy(
    SQLAlchemySyncConfig(
        connection_string="sqlite:///:memory:",
        commit_mode="autocommit",
        create_all=True,
    ),
    app,
)

@app.route("/users")
def list_users() -> dict[str, list[dict[str, object]]]:
    session = alchemy.get_sync_session()
    users = session.execute(select(User)).scalars().all()
    return {"users": [{"id": u.id, "name": u.name} for u in users]}
```

```python
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.flask import SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig

async_app = Flask("flask_async_db")
async_alchemy = AdvancedAlchemy(
    SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(
        connection_string="sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:",
        create_all=True,
    ),
    async_app,
)

@async_app.route("/users")
async def list_users_async() -> dict[str, list[dict[str, object]]]:
    session = async_alchemy.get_async_session()
    users = (await session.execute(select(User))).scalars().all()
    return {"users": [{"id": u.id, "name": u.name} for u in users]}
```

```python
multi_db_app = Flask("flask_multi_db")
multi_alchemy = AdvancedAlchemy(
    [
        SQLAlchemySyncConfig(connection_string="sqlite:///:memory:", bind_key="users"),
        SQLAlchemySyncConfig(connection_string="sqlite:///:memory:", bind_key="products"),
    ],
    multi_db_app,
)

with multi_db_app.app_context():
    users_session = multi_alchemy.get_sync_session("users")
    products_session = multi_alchemy.get_sync_session("products")
```

## Using Services and JSON Responses

Mix `FlaskServiceMixin` into your service class so route handlers can paginate, convert rows to schemas, and return a Flask JSON `Response` in one clean step:

```python
import datetime
from typing import Optional
from uuid import UUID
from flask import Response, request
from msgspec import Struct
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.flask import (
    FlaskServiceMixin,
    filters,
    repository,
    service,
)

class Author(base.UUIDBase):
    __tablename__ = "flask_author"
    name: Mapped[str]
    dob: Mapped[Optional[datetime.date]]

class AuthorSchema(Struct):
    name: str
    id: Optional[UUID] = None
    dob: Optional[datetime.date] = None

class AuthorService(service.SQLAlchemySyncRepositoryService[Author], FlaskServiceMixin):
    class Repo(repository.SQLAlchemySyncRepository[Author]):
        model_type = Author

    repository_type = Repo

service_app = Flask("flask_service_db")
alchemy_config = SQLAlchemySyncConfig(
    connection_string="sqlite:///:memory:",
    commit_mode="autocommit",
    create_all=True,
)
alchemy = AdvancedAlchemy(alchemy_config, service_app)

@service_app.route("/authors", methods=["GET"])
def list_authors() -> Response:
    page = request.args.get("currentPage", 1, type=int)
    size = request.args.get("pageSize", 10, type=int)
    limit_offset = filters.LimitOffset(limit=size, offset=size * (page - 1))

    authors_service = AuthorService(session=alchemy.get_sync_session())
    results, total = authors_service.get_many_and_count(limit_offset)
    payload = authors_service.to_schema(
        results,
        total,
        filters=[limit_offset],
        schema_type=AuthorSchema,
    )
    return authors_service.jsonify(payload)
```

```python
import datetime
from uuid import UUID
from flask import Response, request
from msgspec import Struct
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.flask import (
    FlaskServiceMixin,
    filters,
    repository,
    service,
)

class Author(base.UUIDBase):
    __tablename__ = "flask_author"
    name: Mapped[str]
    dob: Mapped[datetime.date | None]

class AuthorSchema(Struct):
    name: str
    id: UUID | None = None
    dob: datetime.date | None = None

class AuthorService(service.SQLAlchemySyncRepositoryService[Author], FlaskServiceMixin):
    class Repo(repository.SQLAlchemySyncRepository[Author]):
        model_type = Author

    repository_type = Repo

service_app = Flask("flask_service_db")
alchemy_config = SQLAlchemySyncConfig(
    connection_string="sqlite:///:memory:",
    commit_mode="autocommit",
    create_all=True,
)
alchemy = AdvancedAlchemy(alchemy_config, service_app)

@service_app.route("/authors", methods=["GET"])
def list_authors() -> Response:
    page = request.args.get("currentPage", 1, type=int)
    size = request.args.get("pageSize", 10, type=int)
    limit_offset = filters.LimitOffset(limit=size, offset=size * (page - 1))

    authors_service = AuthorService(session=alchemy.get_sync_session())
    results, total = authors_service.get_many_and_count(limit_offset)
    payload = authors_service.to_schema(
        results,
        total,
        filters=[limit_offset],
        schema_type=AuthorSchema,
    )
    return authors_service.jsonify(payload)
```

## Running Migrations with Flask CLI

```bash
flask database init
flask database revision --autogenerate -m "add users table"
flask database upgrade
```

See [Flask](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/flask/index.html) for full API signatures.

Source: https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/usage/frameworks/sanic.html

# Sanic Integration

Advanced Alchemy integrates with Sanic through `sanic-ext`, managing engines on `app.ctx`, creating lazy per-request sessions on `request.ctx`, and injecting `AsyncSession` straight into route handlers.

## What’s Included for Sanic

| Feature | What It Gives You | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **sanic-ext Injection** | Injects `AsyncSession` or `Session` directly into route parameters with `add_session_dependency`. | [API](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/sanic/index.html) |
| **Request Context Sessions** | Lazily opens one session per request on `request.ctx` and cleans it up when the response finishes. | [API](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/sanic/index.html) |
| **Multiple Databases** | Supports multiple sync or async databases side by side using named `bind_key` configs. | [API](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/sanic/index.html) |

## Setup and Route Handlers

```python
from sanic import Sanic
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.sanic import (
    AdvancedAlchemy,
    AsyncSessionConfig,
    SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig,
)

alchemy_config = SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(
    connection_string="sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:",
    session_config=AsyncSessionConfig(expire_on_commit=False),
    create_all=True,
)

app = Sanic("AlchemySanicApp")
alchemy = AdvancedAlchemy(sqlalchemy_config=alchemy_config)
alchemy.register(app)
alchemy.add_session_dependency(AsyncSession)
```

```python
from uuid import UUID
import msgspec
from sanic import HTTPResponse, Request, raw
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.sanic import base, filters, repository, service

class AuthorModel(base.UUIDBase):
    __tablename__ = "sanic_author"
    name: Mapped[str]

class AuthorSchema(msgspec.Struct):
    id: UUID
    name: str

class AuthorService(service.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepositoryService[AuthorModel]):
    class Repo(repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository[AuthorModel]):
        model_type = AuthorModel

    repository_type = Repo

@app.get("/authors")
async def list_authors(request: Request, db_session: AsyncSession) -> HTTPResponse:
    page = int(request.args.get("currentPage", 1))
    size = int(request.args.get("pageSize", 10))
    limit_offset = filters.LimitOffset(limit=size, offset=size * (page - 1))

    authors_service = AuthorService(session=db_session)
    results, total = await authors_service.get_many_and_count(limit_offset)
    payload = authors_service.to_schema(
        results,
        total,
        filters=[limit_offset],
        schema_type=AuthorSchema,
    )
    return raw(msgspec.json.encode(payload), content_type="application/json")
```

```python
from advanced_alchemy.extensions.sanic import SQLAlchemySyncConfig

reporting_app = Sanic("AlchemySanicMultiBindApp")
reporting_alchemy = AdvancedAlchemy(
    sqlalchemy_config=[
        SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(connection_string="sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:"),
        SQLAlchemySyncConfig(connection_string="sqlite+pysqlite:///:memory:", bind_key="reporting"),
    ],
    sanic_app=reporting_app,
)

assert reporting_alchemy.get_config().bind_key == "default"
assert reporting_alchemy.get_config("reporting").bind_key == "reporting"
```

See [Sanic](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/sanic/index.html) for full API signatures.

Source: https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/index.html

# base

## Core Protocols & Attribute Mixins

### `advanced_alchemy.base.ModelProtocol`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.base.ModelProtocol(*args, **kwargs)[source]
```

Bases: `Protocol`

The base SQLAlchemy model protocol.

Defines the minimal contract for a SQLAlchemy-mapped model. Any class with
a mapper and table (including SQLModel `table=True` models) satisfies this protocol.

- **Variables**: - **__table__** – The table associated with the model.
- **__mapper__** – The mapper for the model.

### `advanced_alchemy.base.BasicAttributes`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.base.BasicAttributes[source]
```

Bases: `object`

Basic attributes for SQLAlchemy tables and queries.

Provides a method to convert the model to a dictionary representation.

##### `to_dict`

```python
to_dict()[source]
```

Converts the model to a dictionary, excluding specified fields. :no-index:

### `advanced_alchemy.base.CommonTableAttributes`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.base.CommonTableAttributes[source]
```

Bases: [`BasicAttributes`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/base.html#advanced_alchemy.base.BasicAttributes)

Common attributes for SQLAlchemy tables.

Inherits from [`BasicAttributes`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/base.html#advanced_alchemy.base.BasicAttributes) and provides a mechanism to infer table names from class names
while respecting SQLAlchemy’s inheritance patterns.

This mixin supports all three SQLAlchemy inheritance patterns:
- **Single Table Inheritance (STI)**: Child classes automatically use parent’s table
- **Joined Table Inheritance (JTI)**: Child classes have their own tables with foreign keys
- **Concrete Table Inheritance (CTI)**: Child classes have independent tables

- **Variables**: **__tablename__** – The inferred table name, or `None` for Single Table Inheritance children.

### `advanced_alchemy.base.AdvancedDeclarativeBase`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.base.AdvancedDeclarativeBase(**kwargs)[source]
```

Bases: `DeclarativeBase`

A subclass of declarative base that allows for overriding of the registry.

Inherits from `sqlalchemy.orm.DeclarativeBase`.

- **Variables**: - **registry** – The registry for the declarative base.
- **__metadata_registry__** ([*MetadataRegistry*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/base.html#advanced_alchemy.base.MetadataRegistry)) – The metadata registry.
- **__bind_key__** (*str**|**None*) – The bind key for the metadata.

### `advanced_alchemy.base.SQLQuery`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.base.SQLQuery[source]
```

Bases: [`BasicAttributes`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/base.html#advanced_alchemy.base.BasicAttributes), [`AdvancedDeclarativeBase`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/base.html#advanced_alchemy.base.AdvancedDeclarativeBase), `AsyncAttrs`

Base for all SQLAlchemy custom mapped objects.

> **See Also**: [`BasicAttributes`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/base.html#advanced_alchemy.base.BasicAttributes)
> [`AdvancedDeclarativeBase`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/base.html#advanced_alchemy.base.AdvancedDeclarativeBase)
> `AsyncAttrs`

## Integer & NanoID Declarative Bases

### `advanced_alchemy.base.BigIntBase`


## Registries, Utilities & Type Aliases

### `advanced_alchemy.base.MetadataRegistry`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.base.MetadataRegistry[source]
```

Bases: `object`

A registry for metadata.

Provides methods to get and set metadata for different bind keys.

##### `get`

```python
get(bind_key=None)[source]
```

Get the metadata for the given bind key.

- **Parameters**: **bind_key** (*str**|**None*) – The bind key for the metadata.
- **Returns**: The metadata for the given bind key.
- **Return type**: `sqlalchemy.MetaData`

##### `set`

```python
set(bind_key, metadata)[source]
```

Set the metadata for the given bind key.

- **Parameters**: - **bind_key** (*str**|**None*) – The bind key for the metadata.
- **metadata** (*MetaData*) – The metadata to set.

### `advanced_alchemy.base.create_registry`

```python
advanced_alchemy.base.create_registry(custom_annotation_map=None)[source]
```

Create a new SQLAlchemy registry.

- **Parameters**: **custom_annotation_map** (*dict**[**Any**,**type**[**TypeEngine**]**|**TypeEngine**]**|**None*) – Custom type annotations to use for the registry.
- **Returns**: A new SQLAlchemy registry with the specified type annotations.
- **Return type**: `sqlalchemy.orm.registry`

### `advanced_alchemy.base.merge_table_arguments`

```python
advanced_alchemy.base.merge_table_arguments(cls, table_args=None)[source]
```

Merge Table Arguments.

This function helps merge table arguments when using mixins that include their own table args,
making it easier to append additional information such as comments or constraints to the model.

- **Parameters**: - **cls** (*type**[**DeclarativeBase**]*) – The model that will get the table args.
- **table_args** (*Tuple**[**Any**,**...**]**|**Dict**[**str**,**Any**]**|**None*) – Additional information to add to table_args.
- **Returns**: Merged table arguments.
- **Return type**: [`TableArgsType`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/base.html#advanced_alchemy.base.TableArgsType)

### `advanced_alchemy.base.model_to_dict`

```python
advanced_alchemy.base.model_to_dict(instance, exclude=None)[source]
```

Convert a mapped model instance to a dictionary.

Works with any SQLAlchemy-mapped model, including:
- Advanced Alchemy models (delegates to `to_dict()`)
- SQLModel `table=True` models (uses mapper-based column iteration)
- Any other mapped class

- **Parameters**: - **instance** ([*ModelProtocol*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/base.html#advanced_alchemy.base.ModelProtocol)) – A SQLAlchemy-mapped model instance.
- **exclude** ([*set*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/base.html#advanced_alchemy.base.MetadataRegistry.set)*[**str**]**|**None*) – Optional set of field names to exclude from the output.
- **Returns**: A dictionary of column names to values.
- **Return type**: *dict*[*str*, *Any*]

# unique

### `advanced_alchemy.mixins.unique.UniqueMixin`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.mixins.unique.UniqueMixin[source]
```

Bases: `object`

Mixin for instantiating objects while ensuring uniqueness on some field(s).

This is a slightly modified implementation derived from [https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/wiki/UniqueObject](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/wiki/UniqueObject)

##### `as_unique_async`

```python
async classmethod as_unique_async(session, *args, **kwargs)[source]
```

Instantiate and return a unique object within the provided session based on the given arguments.

If an object with the same unique identifier already exists in the session, it is returned from the cache.

- **Parameters**: - **session** (*Union**[**AsyncSession**,**async_scoped_session**[**AsyncSession**]**]*) – SQLAlchemy async session
- ***args** (*Any*) – Values used to instantiate the instance if no duplicate exists
- ****kwargs** (*Any*) – Values used to instantiate the instance if no duplicate exists
- **Returns**: The unique object instance.
- **Return type**: *Self*

##### `as_unique_sync`

```python
classmethod as_unique_sync(session, *args, **kwargs)[source]
```

Instantiate and return a unique object within the provided session based on the given arguments.

If an object with the same unique identifier already exists in the session, it is returned from the cache.

- **Parameters**: - **session** (*Union**[**Session**,**scoped_session**[**Session**]**]*) – SQLAlchemy sync session
- ***args** (*Any*) – Values used to instantiate the instance if no duplicate exists
- ****kwargs** (*Any*) – Values used to instantiate the instance if no duplicate exists
- **Returns**: The unique object instance.
- **Return type**: *Self*

##### `unique_hash`

```python
classmethod unique_hash(*args, **kwargs)[source]
```

Generate a unique key based on the provided arguments.

This method should be implemented in the subclass.

- **Parameters**: - ***args** (*Any*) – Values passed to the alternate classmethod constructors
- ****kwargs** (*Any*) – Values passed to the alternate classmethod constructors
- **Raises**: **NotImplementedError** – If not implemented in the subclass.
- **Returns**: Any hashable object.
- **Return type**: *Hashable*

##### `unique_filter`

```python
classmethod unique_filter(*args, **kwargs)[source]
```

Generate a filter condition for ensuring uniqueness.

This method should be implemented in the subclass.

- **Parameters**: - ***args** (*Any*) – Values passed to the alternate classmethod constructors
- ****kwargs** (*Any*) – Values passed to the alternate classmethod constructors
- **Raises**: **NotImplementedError** – If not implemented in the subclass.
- **Returns**: Filter condition to establish the uniqueness.
- **Return type**: *ColumnElement*[*bool*]

Source: https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/mixins/nanoid.html

```python
class advanced_alchemy.config.asyncio.AsyncSessionConfig(autobegin=<class 'advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty'>, autoflush=<class 'advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty'>, bind=<class 'advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty'>, binds=<class 'advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty'>, class_=<class 'advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty'>, expire_on_commit=<class 'advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty'>, info=<class 'advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty'>, join_transaction_mode=<class 'advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty'>, query_cls=<class 'advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty'>, twophase=<class 'advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty'>, sync_session_class=<class 'advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty'>)[source]
```

Bases: [`GenericSessionConfig`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/config/common.html#advanced_alchemy.config.common.GenericSessionConfig)␀ [`AsyncConnection`, `AsyncEngine`, `AsyncSession`]

SQLAlchemy async session config.

##### `sync_session_class`

```python
sync_session_class
```

A `Session` subclass or other callable which will be used to construct the
`Session` which will be proxied. This parameter may be used to provide custom
`Session` subclasses. Defaults to the
`AsyncSession.sync_session_class` class-level
attribute.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

### `advanced_alchemy.config.asyncio.SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.config.asyncio.SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(create_engine_callable=<function create_async_engine>, session_config=<factory>, session_maker_class=<class 'sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio.session.async_sessionmaker'>, connection_string=None, engine_config=<factory>, session_maker=None, engine_instance=None, create_all=False, metadata=None, bind_key=None, enable_touch_updated_timestamp_listener=True, enable_file_object_listener=True, file_object_raise_on_error=True, cache_config=None, cache_manager=None, alembic_config=<factory>, routing_config=None)[source]
```

Bases: [`GenericSQLAlchemyConfig`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/config/common.html#advanced_alchemy.config.common.GenericSQLAlchemyConfig)␀ [`AsyncEngine`, `AsyncSession`, `async_sessionmaker`␀ [`AsyncSession`]]

Async SQLAlchemy Configuration.

> **Note**: The alembic configuration options are documented in the Alembic documentation.

> **Example**: Basic async configuration:
>
> ```default
> config = SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(
>     connection_string="postgresql+asyncpg://user:pass@localhost/db",
> )
> ```
>
> Configuration with read/write routing:
>
> ```default
> from advanced_alchemy.config.routing import RoutingConfig
>
> config = SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(
>     routing_config=RoutingConfig(
>         primary_connection_string="postgresql+asyncpg://user:pass@primary/db",
>         read_replicas=[
>             "postgresql+asyncpg://user:pass@replica/db"
>         ],
>     ),
> )
> ```

##### `create_engine_callable`

```python
create_engine_callable(**kw)
```

Callable that creates an `AsyncEngine` instance or instance of its

Disable if you plan to bring your own save/delete mechanism for these columns

Control FileObject error handling behavior.

- `False`: Log warnings on file operation failures, don’t raise exceptions
- `True` (default): Raise exceptions on file operation failures

##### `cache_config`

```python
cache_config: CacheConfig | None = None
```

Optional [`CacheConfig`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/cache.html#advanced_alchemy.cache.CacheConfig) for dogpile.cache integration.

When set, a [`CacheManager`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/cache.html#advanced_alchemy.cache.CacheManager) is instantiated during
`__post_init__` and stored in `session_config.info["cache_manager"]`. Repositories
created against sessions produced by this config will pick the manager up automatically.

Requires the optional `dogpile.cache` dependency (`pip install advanced-alchemy[dogpile]`);
without it the manager falls back to a no-op `NullRegion`.

> **See Also**: [Caching](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/usage/caching.html)

##### `cache_manager`

```python
cache_manager: CacheManager | None = None
```

Takes precedence over [`cache_config`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/config/common.html#advanced_alchemy.config.common.GenericSQLAlchemyConfig.cache_config). Useful when sharing a single cache manager across
multiple configs.

##### `twophase`

```python
twophase
```

When `True`, all transactions will be started as a “two phase” transaction, i.e. using the “two phase”
semantics of the database in use along with an XID. During a `commit()`, after
`flush()` has been issued for all attached databases, the
`TwoPhaseTransaction.prepare()` method on each database`s
`TwoPhaseTransaction` will be called. This allows each database to
roll back the entire transaction, before each transaction is committed.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `connect_args`

```python
connect_args
```

A dictionary of arguments which will be passed directly to the DBAPI’s `connect()` method as keyword arguments.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `echo`

```python
echo
```

If `True`, the Engine will log all statements as well as a `repr()` of their parameter lists to the default
log handler, which defaults to `sys.stdout` for output. If set to the string “debug”, result rows will be printed
to the standard output as well. The echo attribute of Engine can be modified at any time to turn logging on and off;
direct control of logging is also available using the standard Python logging module.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `echo_pool`

```python
echo_pool
```

If `True`, the connection pool will log informational output such as when connections are invalidated as well
as when connections are recycled to the default log handler, which defaults to sys.stdout for output. If set to the
string “debug”, the logging will include pool checkouts and checkins. Direct control of logging is also available
using the standard Python logging module.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `enable_from_linting`

```python
enable_from_linting
```

Defaults to True. Will emit a warning if a given SELECT statement is found to have un-linked FROM elements which
would cause a cartesian product.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `execution_options`

```python
execution_options
```
