alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `hide_parameters`

```python
hide_parameters
```

Boolean, when set to `True`, SQL statement parameters will not be displayed in INFO logging nor will they be
formatted into the string representation of `StatementError` objects.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `insertmanyvalues_page_size`

```python
insertmanyvalues_page_size
```

Number of rows to format into an INSERT statement when the statement uses “insertmanyvalues” mode, which is a
paged form of bulk insert that is used for many backends when using executemany execution typically in conjunction
with RETURNING. Defaults to 1000, but may also be subject to dialect-specific limiting factors which may override
this value on a per-statement basis.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `isolation_level`

```python
isolation_level
```

Optional string name of an isolation level which will be set on all new connections unconditionally. Isolation
levels are typically some subset of the string names “SERIALIZABLE”, “REPEATABLE READ”, “READ COMMITTED”,
“READ UNCOMMITTED” and “AUTOCOMMIT” based on backend.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `json_deserializer`

```python
json_deserializer(*, decode_bytes=True)
```

For dialects that support the `JSON` datatype, this is a Python callable that will
convert a JSON string to a Python object. By default, this is set to
[`advanced_alchemy.utils.serialization.decode_json()`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.serialization.decode_json).

- **Return type**: *Any*

##### `json_serializer`

```python
json_serializer(*, type_encoders=None, as_bytes=False)
```

For dialects that support the JSON datatype, this is a Python callable that will render a given object as JSON.
By default, [`advanced_alchemy.utils.serialization.encode_json()`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.serialization.encode_json) is used.

- **Return type**: *Union*[*str*, *bytes*]

##### `label_length`

```python
label_length
```

Optional integer value which limits the size of dynamically generated column labels to that many characters. If
less than 6, labels are generated as “_(counter)”. If `None`, the value of `dialect.max_identifier_length`,
which may be affected via the `max_identifier_length` parameter of
`sqlalchemy.create_engine()`, is used instead. The value of
`label_length` may not be larger than that of `max_identifier_length`.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `logging_name`

```python
logging_name
```

String identifier which will be used within the “name” field of logging records generated within the
“sqlalchemy.engine” logger. Defaults to a hexstring of the object`s id.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `max_identifier_length`

```python
max_identifier_length
```

Override the max_identifier_length determined by the dialect. if `None` or `0`, has no effect. This is the
database`s configured maximum number of characters that may be used in a SQL identifier such as a table name, column
name, or label name. All dialects determine this value automatically, however in the case of a new database version
for which this value has changed but SQLAlchemy`s dialect has not been adjusted, the value may be passed here.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `max_overflow`

```python
max_overflow
```

The number of connections to allow in connection pool “overflow”, that is connections that can be opened above
and beyond the pool_size setting, which defaults to five. This is only used with
`QueuePool`.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `module`

```python
module
```

Reference to a Python module object (the module itself, not its string name). Specifies an alternate DBAPI module
to be used by the engine`s dialect. Each sub-dialect references a specific DBAPI which will be imported before first
connect. This parameter causes the import to be bypassed, and the given module to be used instead. Can be used for
testing of DBAPIs as well as to inject “mock” DBAPI implementations into the
`Engine`.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `paramstyle`

```python
paramstyle
```

The paramstyle to use when rendering bound parameters. This style defaults to the one recommended by the DBAPI
itself, which is retrieved from the `.paramstyle` attribute of the DBAPI. However, most DBAPIs accept more than
one paramstyle, and in particular it may be desirable to change a “named” paramstyle into a “positional” one, or
vice versa. When this attribute is passed, it should be one of the values “qmark”, “numeric”, “named”, “format” or
“pyformat”, and should correspond to a parameter style known to be supported by the DBAPI in use.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `pool`

```python
pool
```

An already-constructed instance of `Pool`, such as a
`QueuePool` instance. If non-None, this pool will be used directly as the
underlying connection pool for the engine, bypassing whatever connection parameters are present in the URL argument.
For information on constructing connection pools manually, see
[Connection Pooling](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/core/pooling.html).

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `poolclass`

```python
poolclass
```

A `Pool` subclass, which will be used to create a connection pool instance using
the connection parameters given in the URL. Note this differs from pool in that you don`t actually instantiate the
pool in this case, you just indicate what type of pool to be used.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `pool_logging_name`

```python
pool_logging_name
```

String identifier which will be used within the “name” field of logging records generated within the
“sqlalchemy.pool” logger. Defaults to a hexstring of the object`s id.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `pool_pre_ping`

```python
pool_pre_ping
```

If True will enable the connection pool “pre-ping” feature that tests connections for liveness upon each
checkout.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `pool_size`

```python
pool_size
```

The number of connections to keep open inside the connection pool. This used with
`QueuePool` as well as
`SingletonThreadPool`. With
`QueuePool`, a pool_size setting of `0` indicates no limit; to disable pooling,
set `poolclass` to `NullPool` instead.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `pool_recycle`

```python
pool_recycle
```

This setting causes the pool to recycle connections after the given number of seconds has passed. It defaults to
`-1`, or no timeout. For example, setting to `3600` means connections will be recycled after one hour. Note that
MySQL in particular will disconnect automatically if no activity is detected on a connection for eight hours
(although this is configurable with the MySQLDB connection itself and the server configuration as well).

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `pool_reset_on_return`

```python
pool_reset_on_return
```

Set the `Pool.reset_on_return` parameter of the underlying
`Pool` object, which can be set to the values `"rollback"`, `"commit"`, or
`None`.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `pool_timeout`

```python
pool_timeout
```

Number of seconds to wait before giving up on getting a connection from the pool. This is only used with
`QueuePool`. This can be a float but is subject to the limitations of Python time
functions which may not be reliable in the tens of milliseconds.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

##### `pool_use_lifo`

```python
pool_use_lifo
```

Use LIFO (last-in-first-out) when retrieving connections from `QueuePool`
instead of FIFO (first-in-first-out). Using LIFO, a server-side timeout scheme can reduce the number of connections
used during non-peak periods of use. When planning for server-side timeouts, ensure that a recycle or pre-ping
strategy is in use to gracefully handle stale connections.

alias of [`Empty`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)

# cache

Dogpile L2 caching integration for SQLAlchemy repositories with commit-aware
invalidation and per-process singleflight protection.

## Configuration & Region Management

### `advanced_alchemy.cache.CacheConfig`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.cache.CacheConfig(backend='dogpile.cache.null', expiration_time=3600, arguments=<factory>, key_prefix='aa:', enabled=True, serializer=None, deserializer=None, region_factory=None)
```

Bases: `object`

Configuration for a dogpile.cache region.

This dataclass holds configuration options for setting up a cache region
using dogpile.cache. It supports multiple backends (Redis, Memcached, file, memory)
and provides sensible defaults for getting started quickly.

> **Example**: Basic memory cache configuration:
>
> ```default
> config = CacheConfig(
>     backend="dogpile.cache.memory",
>     expiration_time=300,
> )
> ```
>
> Redis cache configuration:
>
> ```default
> config = CacheConfig(
>     backend="dogpile.cache.redis",
>     expiration_time=3600,
>     arguments={
>         "host": "localhost",
>         "port": 6379,
>         "db": 0,
>     },
> )
> ```

##### `backend`

```python
backend: str = 'dogpile.cache.null'
```

Cache backend identifier.

Common backends:
- `dogpile.cache.null`: No-op cache (default, for development)
- `dogpile.cache.memory`: In-process memory cache
- `dogpile.cache.redis`: Redis backend
- `dogpile.cache.memcached`: Memcached backend
- `dogpile.cache.dbm`: DBM file-based cache

##### `expiration_time`

```python
expiration_time: int = 3600
```

Default TTL (time-to-live) in seconds for cached items.

Set to `-1` for no expiration. Default is 3600 (1 hour).

##### `key_prefix`

```python
key_prefix: str = 'aa:'
```

Prefix for all cache keys.

This helps avoid key collisions when sharing a cache backend
with other applications. Default is `aa:` (advanced-alchemy).

##### `enabled`

```python
enabled: bool = True
```

Enable or disable caching globally.

When `False`, all cache operations are bypassed and
data is always fetched from the database. Useful for
debugging or testing.

### `advanced_alchemy.cache.CacheManager`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.cache.CacheManager(config)
```

Bases: `object`

Manages dogpile.cache regions with model-aware invalidation.

This class provides a high-level interface for caching SQLAlchemy model
instances using dogpile.cache. It handles serialization, cache key
generation, and model-version-based invalidation for list queries.

All cache operations are available in both sync and async variants:
- Sync methods end with `_sync` (e.g., `get_sync`, `set_sync`)
- Async methods end with `_async` (e.g., `get_async`, `set_async`)

Async methods use `asyncio.to_thread()` with capacity limiting to
prevent blocking the event loop when using network-based backends
like Redis or Memcached.

Features:
- Lazy initialization of cache regions
- Model-aware cache key generation
- Version-based invalidation for list queries
- Graceful degradation when dogpile.cache is not installed
- Support for custom serializers
- Both sync and async operation support

> **Example**: Sync usage:
>
> ```default
> from advanced_alchemy.cache import CacheConfig, CacheManager
>
> config = CacheConfig(
>     backend="dogpile.cache.memory",
>     expiration_time=300,
> )
> manager = CacheManager(config)
>
> # Cache a value (sync)
> result = manager.get_or_create_sync(
>     "users:1",
>     lambda: fetch_user_from_db(1),
> )
> ```
>
> Async usage:
>
> ```default
> # Cache a value (async)
> result = await manager.get_or_create_async(
>     "users:1",
>     lambda: fetch_user_from_db(1),
> )
> ```

##### `region`

```python
property region: SyncCacheRegionProtocol
```

Get the cache region, creating it if necessary.

The region is lazily initialized on first access. If dogpile.cache
is not installed or initialization fails, returns a NullRegion that
provides the same interface but doesn’t actually cache anything.

- **Returns**: The configured cache region or a NullRegion fallback.

##### `get_sync`

```python
get_sync(key)
```

Get a value from the cache (sync).

- **Parameters**: **key** (*str*) – The cache key (without prefix).
- **Returns**: The cached value or NO_VALUE if not found.
- **Return type**: *object*

##### `set_sync`

```python
set_sync(key, value)
```

Set a value in the cache (sync).

- **Parameters**: - **key** (*str*) – The cache key (without prefix).
- **value** (*Any*) – The value to cache.

##### `delete_sync`

```python
delete_sync(key)
```

Delete a value from the cache (sync).

- **Parameters**: **key** (*str*) – The cache key (without prefix).

##### `get_async`

```python
async get_async(key)
```

Get a value from the cache (async).

- **Parameters**: **key** (*str*) – The cache key (without prefix).
- **Returns**: The cached value or NO_VALUE if not found.
- **Return type**: *object*

##### `set_async`

```python
async set_async(key, value)
```

Set a value in the cache (async).

- **Parameters**: - **key** (*str*) – The cache key (without prefix).
- **value** (*Any*) – The value to cache.

##### `delete_async`

```python
async delete_async(key)
```

Delete a value from the cache (async).

- **Parameters**: **key** (*str*) – The cache key (without prefix).

##### `get_entity_async`

```python
async get_entity_async(model_name, entity_id, model_class, bind_group=None)
```

Get a cached entity by model name and ID (async).

- **Parameters**: - **model_name** (*str*) – The model/table name.
- **entity_id** (*Any*) – The entity’s primary key value.
- **model_class** (*type**[**T**]*) – The SQLAlchemy model class for deserialization.
- **bind_group** (*str**|**None*) – Optional routing group for multi-master configurations.
When provided, entity caches are namespaced by bind_group to
prevent data leaks between database shards/replicas.
- **Returns**: The cached model instance or None if not found.
- **Return type**: *T* | *None*

##### `set_entity_async`

```python
async set_entity_async(model_name, entity_id, entity, bind_group=None)
```

Cache an entity (async).

- **Parameters**: - **model_name** (*str*) – The model/table name.
- **entity_id** (*Any*) – The entity’s primary key value.
- **entity** (*Any*) – The SQLAlchemy model instance to cache.
- **bind_group** (*str**|**None*) – Optional routing group for multi-master configurations.
When provided, entity caches are namespaced by bind_group to
prevent data leaks between database shards/replicas.

##### `invalidate_entity_async`

```python
async invalidate_entity_async(model_name, entity_id, bind_group=None)
```

Invalidate the cache for a specific entity (async).

This should be called after an entity is created, updated, or deleted
to ensure the cache doesn’t serve stale data.

- **Parameters**: - **model_name** (*str*) – The model/table name.
- **entity_id** (*Any*) – The entity’s primary key value.
- **bind_group** (*str**|**None*) – Optional routing group for multi-master configurations.
When provided, only the cache entry for that bind_group is
invalidated.

##### `invalidate_all_async`

```python
async invalidate_all_async()
```

Invalidate all cached values (async).

> **Warning**: This invalidates the entire region, not just keys with
> the configured prefix. Use with caution in shared cache
> environments.

## Serialization & Listeners

### `advanced_alchemy.cache.default_serializer`

```python
advanced_alchemy.cache.default_serializer(model)
```

Serialize a SQLAlchemy model instance to JSON bytes.

This function extracts column values from a SQLAlchemy model and
serializes them to JSON format. The serialized data includes metadata
about the model class for validation during deserialization.

> **Note**: Relationships are NOT serialized. Only column values are included.
> The deserialized object will be a detached instance without
> relationship data loaded.

- **Parameters**: **model** (*Any*) – The SQLAlchemy model instance to serialize.
- **Returns**: JSON-encoded bytes representation of the model.
- **Return type**: *bytes*

> **Example**: Serializing a model:
>
> ```default
> user = User(id=1, name="John", email="john@example.com")
> data = default_serializer(user)
> # b'{"__aa_model__": "User", "__aa_table__": "users", "id": 1, ...}'
> ```

### `advanced_alchemy.cache.default_deserializer`

```python
advanced_alchemy.cache.default_deserializer(data, model_class)
```

Deserialize JSON bytes to a SQLAlchemy model instance.

Creates a new, detached instance of the model class populated with
the serialized column values. The instance is NOT attached to any
session and should be treated as a read-only snapshot.

> **Warning**: The returned instance is detached and does not have relationships
> loaded. Accessing lazy-loaded relationships will raise
> DetachedInstanceError. Use `session.merge()` if you need to
> work with relationships.

- **Parameters**: - **data** (*bytes*) – JSON bytes to deserialize.
- **model_class** (*type**[**T**]*) – The SQLAlchemy model class to instantiate.
- **Returns**: A new, detached instance of the model class.
- **Raises**: **ValueError** – If the serialized data is for a different model class.
- **Return type**: *T*

> **Example**: Deserializing data:
>
> ```default
> data = b'{"__aa_model__": "User", "id": 1, "name": "John"}'
> user = default_deserializer(data, User)
> # user is a detached User instance
> ```

### `advanced_alchemy.cache.setup_cache_listeners`

```python
advanced_alchemy.cache.setup_cache_listeners()
```

Register cache invalidation event listeners globally.

This registers the unified listener on Session, which handles both sync
and async contexts by detecting a running event loop at commit time.
For more control, prefer using scoped listeners via SQLAlchemyConfig.

### `advanced_alchemy.cache.DOGPILE_CACHE_INSTALLED`

```python
advanced_alchemy.cache.DOGPILE_CACHE_INSTALLED: bool
```

Boolean flag indicating whether `dogpile.cache` is installed.

Source: https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/operations.html

# operations

## Upsert & Merge Constructs

### `advanced_alchemy.operations.OnConflictUpsert`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.operations.OnConflictUpsert[source]
```

Bases: `object`

Cross-database upsert operation using dialect-specific constructs.

This class provides a unified interface for upsert operations across
different database backends using their native ON CONFLICT,
ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE, MERGE, or INSERT OR UPDATE mechanisms.

##### `supports_native_upsert`

```python
static supports_native_upsert(dialect_name)[source]
```

Check if the dialect supports the single-row `create_upsert` API.

This flag is scoped to the per-row `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` /
`ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` dialects that
[`OnConflictUpsert.create_upsert()`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/operations.html#advanced_alchemy.operations.OnConflictUpsert.create_upsert) can compile directly. The
bulk `MERGE` (mssql, oracle) and `INSERT OR UPDATE` (spanner)
primitives are dispatched separately by
[`upsert_many()`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository) via [`resolve_upsert_strategy()`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/operations.html#advanced_alchemy.operations.resolve_upsert_strategy)
and are intentionally **not** reported here.

- **Parameters**: **dialect_name** (*str*) – Name of the database dialect
- **Returns**: `True` for postgresql / cockroachdb / sqlite / mysql /
mariadb / duckdb; `False` otherwise.
- **Return type**: *bool*

##### `create_upsert`

```python
static create_upsert(table, values, conflict_columns, update_columns=None, dialect_name=None, validate_identifiers=False)[source]
```

Create a dialect-specific upsert statement.

- **Parameters**: - **table** (*Table*) – Target table for the upsert
- **values** (*dict**[**str**,**Any**]*) – Values to insert/update
- **conflict_columns** ([*list*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository.list)*[**str**]*) – Columns that define the conflict condition
- **update_columns** ([*list*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository.list)*[**str**]**|**None*) – Columns to update on conflict (defaults to all non-conflict columns)
- **dialect_name** (*str**|**None*) – Database dialect name (auto-detected if not provided)
- **validate_identifiers** (*bool*) – If True, validate column names for safety (default: False)
- **Returns**: A SQLAlchemy `Insert` for the ON-CONFLICT dialects (postgresql /
cockroachdb / sqlite / duckdb / mysql / mariadb). MSSQL, Oracle,
and Spanner are handled by the bulk `MERGE` / `INSERT OR UPDATE`
path in [`OnConflictUpsert.create_merge_many()`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/operations.html#advanced_alchemy.operations.OnConflictUpsert.create_merge_many) and
[`OnConflictUpsert.create_insert_or_update_many()`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/operations.html#advanced_alchemy.operations.OnConflictUpsert.create_insert_or_update_many), accessed through
[`resolve_upsert_strategy()`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/operations.html#advanced_alchemy.operations.resolve_upsert_strategy) from the repository layer.
- **Raises**: - **NotImplementedError** – If the dialect doesn’t support native upsert
- **ValueError** – If validate_identifiers is True and invalid identifiers are found
- **Return type**: *Insert*

##### `create_insert_or_update_many`

```python
static create_insert_or_update_many(table, rows)[source]
```

Create a Spanner `INSERT OR UPDATE` using SQLAlchemy’s Insert.

A regular `Insert` retains result-column
metadata, allowing callers to add `returning(model_type)`. The
Spanner dialect compiles that combination to `THEN RETURN`.

- **Parameters**: - **table** (*Table*) – Target table for the upsert.
- **rows** (*Sequence**[**dict**[**str**,**Any**]**]*) – Homogeneous rows to insert or update.
- **Returns**: A multi-values insert prefixed with Spanner’s `OR UPDATE` token.
- **Raises**: **ValueError** – `rows` is empty or rows have heterogeneous keys.
- **Return type**: *Insert*

##### `create_merge_upsert`

```python
static create_merge_upsert(table, values, conflict_columns, update_columns=None, dialect_name=None, validate_identifiers=False)[source]
```

Create a MERGE-based upsert for Oracle/PostgreSQL 15+.

For Oracle databases, this method automatically generates values for primary key
columns that have callable defaults (such as UUID generation functions). This is
necessary because Oracle MERGE statements cannot use Python callable defaults
directly in the INSERT clause. Since Oracle requires `FROM DUAL` for `SELECT`
statements without tables, the Oracle source subquery selects from `DUAL`.

- **Parameters**: - **table** (*Table*) – Target table for the upsert
- **values** (*dict**[**str**,**Any**]*) – Values to insert/update
- **conflict_columns** ([*list*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository.list)*[**str**]*) – Columns that define the matching condition
- **update_columns** ([*list*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository.list)*[**str**]**|**None*) – Columns to update on match (defaults to all non-conflict columns)
- **dialect_name** (*str**|**None*) – Database dialect name (used to determine Oracle-specific syntax)
- **validate_identifiers** (*bool*) – If True, validate column names for safety (default: False)
- **Returns**: A tuple of (MergeStatement, additional_params) where additional_params
contains any generated values (like Oracle UUID primary keys)
- **Raises**: **ValueError** – If validate_identifiers is True and invalid identifiers are found
- **Return type**: *tuple*[[*MergeStatement*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/operations.html#advanced_alchemy.operations.MergeStatement), *dict*[*str*, *Any*]]

##### `create_upsert_many`

```python
static create_upsert_many(table, rows, conflict_columns, update_columns=None, dialect_name=None, validate_identifiers=False, model_type=None)[source]
```

Build a dialect-specific bulk Insert with ON CONFLICT / ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE.

Compiles to a single `INSERT ... VALUES (...), (...), ...` per chunk so the
round-trip cost is fixed regardless of batch size.

- **Parameters**: - **table** (*Table*) – Target table for the upsert.
- **rows** (*Sequence**[**dict**[**str**,**Any**]**]*) – Rows to insert/update. All rows MUST share the same keys.
- **conflict_columns** ([*list*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository.list)*[**str**]*) – Columns that define the conflict / match condition.
- **update_columns** ([*list*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository.list)*[**str**]**|**None*) – Columns to update on conflict (defaults to all
non-conflict keys from the first row).
- **dialect_name** (*str**|**None*) – Database dialect name; determines compile path.
- **validate_identifiers** (*bool*) – If True, validate column identifiers for safety.
- **model_type** (*type**[**Any**]**|**None*) – Optional ORM model target used for ORM-aware RETURNING.
- **Returns**: A SQLAlchemy `Insert` statement configured for bulk upsert.
- **Raises**: - **ValueError** – `rows` is empty, rows have heterogeneous keys,
 or identifier validation fails.
- **NotImplementedError** – The dialect does not support an ON CONFLICT
 style native bulk upsert.
- **Return type**: *Insert*

##### `create_merge_many`

```python
static create_merge_many(table, rows, conflict_columns, update_columns=None, dialect_name=None, validate_identifiers=False)[source]
```

Build a multi-row `MergeStatement` for dialects with native MERGE support.

- **Parameters**: - **table** (*Table*) – Target table for the upsert.
- **rows** (*Sequence**[**dict**[**str**,**Any**]**]*) – Rows to insert/update. All rows MUST share the same keys.
- **conflict_columns** ([*list*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository.list)*[**str**]*) – Columns that define the matching condition.
- **update_columns** ([*list*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository.list)*[**str**]**|**None*) – Columns to update on match (defaults to all non-conflict
keys from the first row).
- **dialect_name** (*str**|**None*) – Database dialect name; selects the source construction.
- **validate_identifiers** (*bool*) – If True, validate column identifiers for safety.
- **Returns**: A single [`MergeStatement`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/operations.html#advanced_alchemy.operations.MergeStatement) binding all input rows.
- **Raises**: - **ValueError** – `rows` is empty, rows have heterogeneous keys,
 or identifier validation fails.
- **NotImplementedError** – The dialect does not support bulk MERGE compilation.
- **Return type**: [*MergeStatement*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/operations.html#advanced_alchemy.operations.MergeStatement)

### `advanced_alchemy.operations.MergeStatement`

Bases: `Executable`, `ClauseElement`

## Strategy Resolution & Validation

### `advanced_alchemy.operations.UpsertStrategy`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.operations.UpsertStrategy(kind, supports_returning, conflict_columns, dialect_name)[source]
```

Bases: `NamedTuple`

Dispatch decision returned by [`resolve_upsert_strategy()`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/operations.html#advanced_alchemy.operations.resolve_upsert_strategy).

Tells the repository which native primitive to compile (`on_conflict` /
`merge` / `insert_or_update`) or whether to take the existing
SELECT-then-partition fallback. The `conflict_columns` field is the
*validated* unique key (PK / UniqueConstraint / unique Index) and has
exactly the same columns as the caller’s `match_fields`.

##### `kind`

```python
kind: 'on_conflict' | 'merge' | 'insert_or_update' | 'fallback'
```

Alias for field number 0

##### `supports_returning`

```python
supports_returning: bool
```

Alias for field number 1

##### `conflict_columns`

```python
conflict_columns: tuple[str, ...]
```

Alias for field number 2

##### `dialect_name`

```python
dialect_name: str
```

Alias for field number 3

### `advanced_alchemy.operations.resolve_upsert_strategy`

```python
advanced_alchemy.operations.resolve_upsert_strategy(table, match_fields, dialect)[source]
```

Resolve the optimal upsert strategy for `(table, match_fields, dialect)`.

The result is cached for the process lifetime; `Table` objects are
singletons per declarative class, so this is one decision per
`(model, match_fields, dialect)` tuple.

Resolution priority:

1. `match_fields` equals the table’s primary key →
native primitive for the dialect, `conflict_columns` is the PK.
2. A `UniqueConstraint` whose columns match exactly →
native primitive where the backend can target it, `conflict_columns`
is that constraint’s columns.
3. A unique `Index` whose columns match exactly →
native primitive where the backend can target it, `conflict_columns`
is that index’s columns. Spanner `INSERT OR UPDATE` only matches the
primary key, and ambiguous MySQL/MariaDB unique targets fall back.
4. Otherwise → `kind="fallback"`, `supports_returning=False`. This
includes `match_fields` entries that do not resolve to table columns
(mapped attributes whose name differs from the column key, synonyms,
hybrids) — the ORM fallback resolves those via `getattr`.

- **Parameters**: - **table** (*Table*) – Target table. Used by identity for caching.
- **match_fields** (*Sequence**[**str**]*) – Columns the caller wants to match on. Order-insensitive.
- **dialect** (*str**|**Dialect*) – Database dialect or dialect name. Passing the runtime dialect
allows the resolver to honor its actual RETURNING capability.
- **Returns**: An [`UpsertStrategy`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/operations.html#advanced_alchemy.operations.UpsertStrategy) describing the decision.
- **Raises**: **ValueError** – `match_fields` is empty.
- **Return type**: [*UpsertStrategy*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/operations.html#advanced_alchemy.operations.UpsertStrategy)

### `advanced_alchemy.operations.resolve_column_default`

```python
advanced_alchemy.operations.resolve_column_default(arg)[source]
```

Invoke a SQLAlchemy `ColumnDefault.arg` callable, tolerating both signatures.

SQLAlchemy accepts both context-taking defaults (`lambda ctx: …`) and
zero-arg defaults (`lambda: …`, `uuid7`, `datetime.utcnow`). The
context-taking shape is attempted first with `None`; a signature
mismatch retries the zero-arg shape. Errors raised inside the default
itself — including a context-sensitive default that dereferences the
`None` context — propagate so callers can route the operation through
the ORM flush, where a real execution context is available.

- **Return type**: *Any*

### `advanced_alchemy.operations.validate_identifier`

```python
advanced_alchemy.operations.validate_identifier(name, identifier_type='identifier')[source]
```

Validate a SQL identifier to ensure it’s safe for use in SQL statements.

This function provides validation for SQL identifiers
(table names, column names, etc.) to ensure they contain only safe characters.
While the operations in this module should only receive identifiers from
trusted sources, this validation adds an extra layer of security.

Note: SQL keywords (like ‘select’, ‘insert’, etc.) are allowed as they can
be properly quoted/escaped by SQLAlchemy when used as identifiers.

- **Parameters**: - **name** (*str*) – The identifier to validate
- **identifier_type** (*str*) – Type of identifier for error messages (e.g., “column”, “table”)
- **Returns**: The validated identifier
- **Raises**: **ValueError** – If the identifier is empty or contains invalid characters
- **Return type**: *str*

### `advanced_alchemy.operations.UpsertKind`

```python
advanced_alchemy.operations.UpsertKind: TypeAlias
```

Literal union of supported dialect upsert execution strategies.

Source: https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/types.html

# types

## Identifiers, Timestamps & JSON Types

### `advanced_alchemy.types.GUID`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.types.GUID(*args, binary=True, **kwargs)
```

Bases: `TypeDecorator`

Platform-independent GUID type.

Uses PostgreSQL’s UUID type (Postgres, DuckDB, Cockroach),
MSSQL’s UNIQUEIDENTIFIER type, Oracle’s RAW(16) or CHAR(32) type,
otherwise uses BINARY(16) or CHAR(32),
storing as stringified hex values.

Will accept stringified UUIDs as a hexstring or an actual UUID

### `advanced_alchemy.types.DateTimeUTC`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.types.DateTimeUTC(*args, fsp=None, precision=None, timezone=True, **kwargs)
```

Bases: `TypeDecorator`

Timezone Aware DateTime.

Ensure UTC is stored in the database and that TZ aware dates are returned for all dialects.

> **Note**: On MySQL/MariaDB and Oracle, omitting `fsp` currently compiles to a whole-second column
> type (`DATETIME` on MySQL/MariaDB and `DATE` on Oracle) and emits a
> `DeprecationWarning`. Pass `fsp=6` to preserve microsecond precision, or
> `fsp=0` to explicitly retain whole-second precision. In v2.0, `fsp=6` will become
> the default.

### `advanced_alchemy.types.BigIntIdentity`

### `advanced_alchemy.types.MutableList`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.types.MutableList(*args, **kwargs)
```

Bases: `MutableList`␀ [`T`]

A list type that implements `Mutable`.

The [`MutableList`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/types.html#advanced_alchemy.types.MutableList) object implements a list that will
emit change events to the underlying mapping when the contents of
the list are altered, including when values are added or removed.

This is a replication of default Mutablelist provide by SQLAlchemy.
The difference here is the properties _removed which keep every element
removed from the list in order to be able to delete them after commit
and keep them when session rolled back.

### `advanced_alchemy.types.FileObject`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.types.FileObject(backend, filename, to_filename=None, content_type=None, size=None, last_modified=None, checksum=None, etag=None, version_id=None, metadata=None, source_path=None, content=None)
```

Bases: `object`

Represents file metadata during processing using a dataclass structure.

This class provides a unified interface for handling file metadata and operations
across different storage backends.

Content or a source path can optionally be provided during initialization via kwargs, store it internally, and add save/save_async methods to persist this pending data using the configured backend.

##### `save`

```python
save(data=None, *, use_multipart=None, chunk_size=5 * 1024 * 1024, max_concurrency=12)
```

Save data to the storage backend using this FileObject’s metadata.

If `data` is provided, it is used directly.
If `data` is None, checks internal source_content or source_path.
Clears pending attributes after successful save.

- **Parameters**: - **data** (*IO**[**bytes**]**|**Path**|**bytes**|**Iterator**[**bytes**]**|**Iterable**[**bytes**]**|**None*) – Optional data to save (bytes, iterator, file-like, Path). If None,
internal pending data is used.
- **use_multipart** (*bool**|**None*) – Passed to the backend’s save method.
- **chunk_size** (*int*) – Passed to the backend’s save method.
- **max_concurrency** (*int*) – Passed to the backend’s save method.
- **Returns**: The updated FileObject instance returned by the backend.
- **Raises**: **TypeError** – If trying to save async data synchronously.
- **Return type**: [*FileObject*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/types.html#advanced_alchemy.types.FileObject)

##### `save_async`

```python
async save_async(data=None, *, use_multipart=None, chunk_size=5 * 1024 * 1024, max_concurrency=12)
```

Save data to the storage backend asynchronously.

If `data` is provided, it is used directly.
If `data` is None, checks internal source_content or source_path.
Clears pending attributes after successful save.
Uses asyncio.to_thread for reading source_path if backend doesn’t handle Path directly.

- **Parameters**: - **data** (*IO**[**bytes**]**|**Path**|**bytes**|**AsyncIterator**[**bytes**]**|**AsyncIterable**[**bytes**]**|**Iterator**[**bytes**]**|**Iterable**[**bytes**]**|**None*) – Optional data to save (bytes, async iterator, file-like, Path, etc.).
If None, internal pending data is used.
- **use_multipart** (*bool**|**None*) – Passed to the backend’s async save method.
- **chunk_size** (*int*) – Passed to the backend’s async save method.
- **max_concurrency** (*int*) – Passed to the backend’s async save method.
- **Returns**: The updated FileObject instance returned by the backend.
- **Raises**: **TypeError** – If trying to save sync data asynchronously.
- **Return type**: [*FileObject*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/types.html#advanced_alchemy.types.FileObject)

## Encryption & Password Hashing

### `advanced_alchemy.types.EncryptedString`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.types.EncryptedString(key=DEFAULT_ENCRYPTION_KEY, backend=FernetBackend, length=None, **kwargs)
```

Bases: `TypeDecorator`

SQLAlchemy TypeDecorator for storing encrypted string values in a database.

This type provides transparent encryption/decryption of string values using the specified backend.
It extends `sqlalchemy.types.TypeDecorator` and implements String as its underlying type.

- **Parameters**: - **key** (*Union**[**str**,**bytes**,**Callable**[**[**]**,**Union**[**str**,**bytes**]**]**]*) – The encryption key. Can be a string, bytes, or callable returning either. Defaults to `os.urandom(32)`.
- **backend** (*type**[*[*EncryptionBackend*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/types.html#advanced_alchemy.types.EncryptionBackend)*]*) – The encryption backend class to use. Defaults to [`FernetBackend`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/types.html#advanced_alchemy.types.FernetBackend).
- **length** (*Optional**[**int**]*) – The length of the unencrypted string. This is used for documentation and validation purposes only, as encrypted strings will be longer.
- ****kwargs** (*Any*) – Additional arguments passed to the underlying String type.
- **Variables**: - **key** – The encryption key.
- **backend** – The encryption backend instance.
- **length** – The unencrypted string length.

### `advanced_alchemy.types.EncryptedText`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.types.EncryptedText
```

Bases: [`EncryptedString`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/types.html#advanced_alchemy.types.EncryptedString)

SQLAlchemy TypeDecorator for storing encrypted text/CLOB values in a database.

This type provides transparent encryption/decryption of text values using the specified backend.
It extends [`EncryptedString`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/types.html#advanced_alchemy.types.EncryptedString) and implements Text as its underlying type.
This is suitable for storing larger encrypted text content compared to EncryptedString.

- **Parameters**: - **key** (*Union**[**str**,**bytes**,**Callable**[**[**]**,**Union**[**str**,**bytes**]**]**]*) – The encryption key. Can be a string, bytes, or callable returning either. Defaults to `os.urandom(32)`.
- **backend** (*type**[*[*EncryptionBackend*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/types.html#advanced_alchemy.types.EncryptionBackend)*]*) – The encryption backend class to use. Defaults to [`FernetBackend`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/types.html#advanced_alchemy.types.FernetBackend).
- ****kwargs** (*Any*) – Additional arguments passed to the underlying String type.

### `advanced_alchemy.types.EncryptionBackend`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.types.EncryptionBackend
```

Bases: `ABC`

Abstract base class for encryption backends.

This class defines the interface that all encryption backends must implement.
Concrete implementations should provide the actual encryption/decryption logic.

- **Variables**: **passphrase** – The encryption passphrase used by the backend.

### `advanced_alchemy.types.FernetBackend`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.types.FernetBackend
```

Bases: [`EncryptionBackend`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/types.html#advanced_alchemy.types.EncryptionBackend)

Fernet-based encryption backend.

This backend uses the Python cryptography library’s Fernet implementation
for encryption/decryption operations. Provides authenticated symmetric
encryption (AES-128-CBC + HMAC-SHA256). The key is derived from the
provided passphrase with a single SHA256 digest.

- **Variables**: - **key** – The base64-encoded key used for encryption and decryption.
- **fernet** – The Fernet instance used for encryption/decryption.

### `advanced_alchemy.types.PGCryptoBackend`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.types.PGCryptoBackend
```

Bases: [`EncryptionBackend`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/types.html#advanced_alchemy.types.EncryptionBackend)

PostgreSQL pgcrypto-based encryption backend.

This backend uses PostgreSQL’s pgcrypto extension for encryption/decryption operations.
Requires the pgcrypto extension to be installed in the database. Encryption and
decryption run server-side via [`bind_expression()`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/types.html#advanced_alchemy.types.PGCryptoBackend) and [`column_expression()`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/types.html#advanced_alchemy.types.PGCryptoBackend);
the ASCII-armored ciphertext is stored as text so the column type is unchanged.

- **Variables**: **passphrase** – The base64-encoded passphrase used for encryption and decryption.

### `advanced_alchemy.types.PasswordHash`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.types.PasswordHash(backend, length=255)
```

Bases: `TypeDecorator`

SQLAlchemy TypeDecorator for storing hashed passwords in a database.

This type provides transparent hashing of password values using the specified backend.
It extends `sqlalchemy.types.TypeDecorator` and implements String as its underlying type.

## One-Time Codes & TOTP

### `advanced_alchemy.types.OneTimeCode`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.types.OneTimeCode(backend, ttl_seconds=None, max_attempts=3, **kwargs)
```

Bases: `TypeDecorator`

Stores a transient one-time code hashed, with expiry and single-use state in JSON.

The column holds `{"hash", "expires_at", "used_at", "attempts"}` so the full lifecycle
lives in one value: an expired or already-redeemed code fails verification, and the code
can lock after `max_attempts` failures. Reads return a [`HashedOneTimeCode`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/types.html#advanced_alchemy.types.HashedOneTimeCode).
Requires an explicit backend.

### `advanced_alchemy.types.HashedOneTimeCode`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.types.HashedOneTimeCode(hash_string, backend, *, expires_at=None, used_at=None, attempts=0, max_attempts=None)
```

Bases: `object`

Read-side wrapper over a stored one-time code’s hash and lifecycle state.

`verify` only succeeds while the code is still redeemable (not expired, not used, and
not locked out). State transitions return a new instance to assign back to the column;
commit it to persist single-use and attempt tracking.

### `advanced_alchemy.types.generate_one_time_code`

```python
advanced_alchemy.types.generate_one_time_code(length=6, *, digits_only=True)
```

Generate a cryptographically secure random one-time code.

- **Parameters**: - **length** (*int*) – Number of characters in the code. Defaults to 6.
- **digits_only** (*bool*) – Use digits only when True (default); otherwise uppercase letters and digits.
- **Returns**: A random one-time code string.
- **Return type**: *str*

### `advanced_alchemy.types.TOTPSecret`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.types.TOTPSecret(key, backend=FernetBackend, digits=6, interval=30, digest=None, issuer=None, length=None, **kwargs)
```

Bases: [`EncryptedString`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/types.html#advanced_alchemy.types.EncryptedString)

Stores a TOTP shared secret encrypted at rest, returning a [`TOTPProvider`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/types.html#advanced_alchemy.types.TOTPProvider) on read.

Storage is identical to [`EncryptedString`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/types.html#advanced_alchemy.types.EncryptedString); the read side wraps the decrypted secret
in a [`TOTPProvider`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/types.html#advanced_alchemy.types.TOTPProvider) so callers can generate and verify codes. Requires `pyotp`.

### `advanced_alchemy.types.TOTPProvider`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.types.TOTPProvider(secret, *, digits=6, interval=30, digest=None, issuer=None)
```

Bases: `object`

Read-side wrapper exposing pyotp operations over a decrypted secret.

The secret must be a valid base32 string. pyotp decodes it lazily, so a malformed
secret raises `binascii.Error` on the first call that decodes it (`now`/`verify`).

### `advanced_alchemy.types.generate_totp_secret`

```python
advanced_alchemy.types.generate_totp_secret(length=32)
```

Generate a new random base32 TOTP secret.

- **Parameters**: **length** (*int*) – Number of base32 characters. Defaults to 32.
- **Raises**: [**MissingDependencyError**](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.MissingDependencyError) – If the `pyotp` package is not installed.
- **Returns**: A base32-encoded secret suitable for an authenticator app.
- **Return type**: *str*

Source: https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html

# exceptions

Exception hierarchy and SQLAlchemy error translation utilities converting
low-level driver errors such as `sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError` and
`sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError` into typed domain exceptions.

## Base & Configuration Exceptions

### `advanced_alchemy.exceptions.AdvancedAlchemyError`

```python
exception advanced_alchemy.exceptions.AdvancedAlchemyError(*args, detail='')[source]
```

Bases: `Exception`

Base exception class from which all Advanced Alchemy exceptions inherit.

### `advanced_alchemy.exceptions.ImproperConfigurationError`

```python
exception advanced_alchemy.exceptions.ImproperConfigurationError[source]
```

Bases: [`AdvancedAlchemyError`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.AdvancedAlchemyError)

Improper Configuration error.

This exception is raised when there is an issue with the configuration of a module.

- **Parameters**: - ***args** (*Any*) – Variable length argument list passed to parent class.
- **detail** (*str*) – Detailed error message.

### `advanced_alchemy.exceptions.MissingDependencyError`

```python
exception advanced_alchemy.exceptions.MissingDependencyError(package, install_package=None)[source]
```

Bases: [`AdvancedAlchemyError`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.AdvancedAlchemyError), `ImportError`

Missing optional dependency.

This exception is raised when a module depends on a dependency that has not been installed.

- **Parameters**: - **package** (*str*) – Name of the missing package.
- **install_package** (*str**|**None*) – Optional alternative package name to install.


Encoding or decoding error.

This exception is raised when serialization or deserialization of an object fails.

- **Parameters**: - ***args** (*Any*) – Variable length argument list passed to parent class.
- **detail** (*str*) – Detailed error message.

## Exception Translation & Error Templates

### `advanced_alchemy.exceptions.ErrorMessages`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.exceptions.ErrorMessages[source]
```

Bases: `TypedDict`

Custom error message templates or callables keyed by error category.

##### `duplicate_key`

```python
duplicate_key: str | Callable[[Exception], str]
```

Error message or callable for duplicate key constraint violations.

##### `integrity`

```python
integrity: str | Callable[[Exception], str]
```

Error message or callable for general integrity constraint violations.

##### `foreign_key`

```python
foreign_key: str | Callable[[Exception], str]
```

Error message or callable for foreign key constraint violations.

##### `multiple_rows`

```python
multiple_rows: str | Callable[[Exception], str]
```

Error message or callable for queries returning multiple rows when one was expected.

##### `check_constraint`

```python
check_constraint: str | Callable[[Exception], str]
```

Error message or callable for check constraint violations.

##### `other`

```python
other: str | Callable[[Exception], str]
```

Error message or callable for unclassified repository exceptions.

##### `not_found`

```python
not_found: str | Callable[[Exception], str]
```

Error message or callable when no matching row is found.

### `advanced_alchemy.exceptions.wrap_sqlalchemy_exception`

```python
advanced_alchemy.exceptions.wrap_sqlalchemy_exception(error_messages=None, dialect_name=None, wrap_exceptions=True)[source]
```

Do something within context to raise a `RepositoryError` chained
from an original `SQLAlchemyError`.

- **Parameters**: - **error_messages** ([*ErrorMessages*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.ErrorMessages)*|**None*) – Error messages to use for the exception.
- **dialect_name** (*str**|**None*) – The name of the dialect to use for the exception.
- **wrap_exceptions** (*bool*) – Wrap SQLAlchemy exceptions in a `RepositoryError`. When set to `False`, the original exception will be raised.
- **Raises**: - [**NotFoundError**](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.NotFoundError) – Raised when no rows matched the specified data.
- **MultipleResultsFound** – Raised when multiple rows matched the specified data.
- [**IntegrityError**](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.IntegrityError) – Raised when an integrity error occurs.
- [**InvalidRequestError**](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.InvalidRequestError) – Raised when an invalid request was made to SQLAlchemy.
- [**RepositoryError**](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.RepositoryError) – Raised for other SQLAlchemy errors.
- **AttributeError** – Raised when an attribute error occurs during processing.
- **SQLAlchemyError** – Raised for general SQLAlchemy errors.
- **StatementError** – Raised when there is an issue processing the statement.
- [**MultipleResultsFoundError**](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.MultipleResultsFoundError) – Raised when multiple rows matched the specified data.
- **Return type**: *Generator*[*None*, *None*, *None*]

Source: https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/cli.html

# cli

Command-line interface and migration commands for Advanced Alchemy.

## CLI Commands

### alchemy

Advanced Alchemy CLI commands.

```shell
alchemy [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

##### `,<config>-c--config`

```text
-c, --config <config>
```

Dotted or colon path to SQLAlchemy config(s) or factory callable (env: ALCHEMY_CONFIG)

##### `--validate-config`

```text
--validate-config
```

Validate configuration before executing migrations

#### `ALCHEMY_CONFIG`

```text
ALCHEMY_CONFIG
```

> Provide a default for [`--config`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/cli.html#cmdoption-alchemy-c)

## Configuration & Discovery Helpers

### `advanced_alchemy.cli.add_migration_commands`

```python
advanced_alchemy.cli.add_migration_commands(database_group=None)[source]
```

Add migration commands to the database group.

- **Parameters**: **database_group** (*Group**|**None*) – The database group to add the commands to.
- **Returns**: The database group with the migration commands added.
- **Return type**: Group

### `advanced_alchemy.cli.get_alchemy_group`

```python
advanced_alchemy.cli.get_alchemy_group()[source]
```

Get the Advanced Alchemy CLI group.

- **Raises**: [**MissingDependencyError**](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.MissingDependencyError) – If the `click` package is not installed.
- **Returns**: The Advanced Alchemy CLI group.
- **Return type**: Group

### `advanced_alchemy.cli.discover_config_from_pyproject`

```python
advanced_alchemy.cli.discover_config_from_pyproject()[source]
```

Find and parse `pyproject.toml` for Advanced Alchemy CLI configuration.

Walks upward from the current working directory to locate `pyproject.toml`
and parses `[tool.advanced-alchemy]` (or `[tool.advanced_alchemy]` /
`[tool.alchemy]`) for the `config` key.

- **Returns**: Configured path string (comma-separated when configured as a list), or
`None` when not found.
- **Return type**: *str* | *None*

### `advanced_alchemy.cli.find_pyproject_toml`

```python
advanced_alchemy.cli.find_pyproject_toml()[source]
```

Walk the filesystem upward from `Path.cwd()` to find `pyproject.toml`.

Stops at a `.git` directory boundary (repository root) or the filesystem root.

- **Returns**: Path to `pyproject.toml`, or `None` if not found.
- **Return type**: *Path* | *None*

### `advanced_alchemy.cli.parse_pyproject_config`

```python
advanced_alchemy.cli.parse_pyproject_config(pyproject_path)[source]
```

Parse `pyproject.toml` for Advanced Alchemy CLI configuration.

Checks `[tool.advanced-alchemy]`, `[tool.advanced_alchemy]`, and
`[tool.alchemy]` in order for a `config` entry.

- **Parameters**: **pyproject_path** (*Path*) – Path to the `pyproject.toml` file.
- **Returns**: Config path(s) as a string (converting a list of strings to a
comma-separated string), or `None` if no config is defined.
- **Raises**: **ValueError** – If the `pyproject.toml` file cannot be parsed or the
 `config` value is not a string or list of strings.
- **Return type**: *str* | *None*

### `advanced_alchemy.cli.resolve_config_async`

```python
async advanced_alchemy.cli.resolve_config_async(config_path)[source]
```

Resolve configuration asynchronously from a dotted or colon-separated path.

Supports direct config instances, sequences of configs, wrapper objects exposing
`.config` (such as `SQLAlchemyInitPlugin` or `AdvancedAlchemy`), synchronous
factory callables, and asynchronous coroutine factories.

- **Parameters**: **config_path** (*str*) – `module.attribute` or `module:attribute` path to a config
object or factory callable.
- **Returns**: A resolved config instance or list of config instances.
- **Raises**: [**ImproperConfigurationError**](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.ImproperConfigurationError) – If importing, executing, or validating the
 configuration fails.
- **Return type**: *Union*[[*list*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository.list)[*Union*[[*SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/config/asyncio.html#advanced_alchemy.config.asyncio.SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig), [*SQLAlchemySyncConfig*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/config/sync.html#advanced_alchemy.config.sync.SQLAlchemySyncConfig)]], [*SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/config/asyncio.html#advanced_alchemy.config.asyncio.SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig), [*SQLAlchemySyncConfig*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/config/sync.html#advanced_alchemy.config.sync.SQLAlchemySyncConfig)]

### `advanced_alchemy.cli.resolve_config_sync`

```python
advanced_alchemy.cli.resolve_config_sync(config_path)[source]
```

Resolve configuration synchronously from a dotted or colon-separated path.

Supports direct config instances, sequences of configs, wrapper objects exposing
`.config` (such as `SQLAlchemyInitPlugin` or `AdvancedAlchemy`), synchronous
factory callables, and asynchronous coroutine factories.

- **Parameters**: **config_path** (*str*) – `module.attribute` or `module:attribute` path to a config
object or factory callable.
- **Returns**: A resolved config instance or list of config instances.
- **Raises**: [**ImproperConfigurationError**](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.ImproperConfigurationError) – If importing, executing, or validating the
 configuration fails.

### `advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.simple_asdict`

```python
advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.simple_asdict(obj, exclude_none=False, exclude_empty=False, convert_nested=True, exclude=None)[source]
```

Convert a dataclass to a dictionary.

This method has important differences to the standard library version:
- it does not deepcopy values
- it does not recurse into collections

- **Parameters**: - **obj** ([*DataclassProtocol*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.DataclassProtocol)) – [`DataclassProtocol`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.DataclassProtocol) instance.
- **exclude_none** (*bool*) – Whether to exclude None values.
- **exclude_empty** (*bool*) – Whether to exclude Empty values.
- **convert_nested** (*bool*) – Whether to recursively convert nested dataclasses.
- **exclude** (*Optional**[**AbstractSet**[**str**]**]*) – An iterable of fields to exclude.
- **Returns**: A dictionary of key/value pairs.
- **Return type**: *dict*[*str*, *Any*]

### `advanced_alchemy.utils.serialization.decode_json`

```python
advanced_alchemy.utils.serialization.decode_json(data, *, decode_bytes=True)[source]
```

Decode JSON string or bytes to Python object.

- **Parameters**: - **data** (*Union**[**str**,**bytes**]*) – JSON string or bytes to decode.
- **decode_bytes** (*bool*) – If True, decode bytes input. If False, bytes
are returned as-is without decoding.
- **Returns**: Decoded Python object.
- **Return type**: *Any*

### `advanced_alchemy.utils.serialization.encode_json`

```python
advanced_alchemy.utils.serialization.encode_json(data, *, type_encoders=None, as_bytes=False)[source]
```

Encode data to JSON with optional custom type encoders.

This is the primary interface for JSON encoding in Advanced Alchemy.
It supports custom type encoders that can be passed per-call.

- **Parameters**: - **data** (*Any*) – Data to encode to JSON.
- **type_encoders** (*Optional**[*[*TypeEncodersMap*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/config/types.html#advanced_alchemy.config.types.TypeEncodersMap)*]*) – Optional mapping of types to encoder functions.
These are merged with DEFAULT_TYPE_ENCODERS, with user
encoders taking precedence.
- **as_bytes** (*bool*) – If True, return bytes; otherwise return str.
- **Returns**: JSON representation of data as string or bytes.
- **Return type**: *Union*[*str*, *bytes*]

### `advanced_alchemy.utils.fixtures.open_fixture`

```python
advanced_alchemy.utils.fixtures.open_fixture(fixtures_path, fixture_name)[source]
```

Loads JSON or CSV file with the specified fixture name.

Supports plain files, gzipped files (.json.gz, .csv.gz), and zipped files (.json.zip, .csv.zip).
The function automatically detects the file format based on file extension and handles
decompression transparently. JSON files take priority over CSV files. Supports both
lowercase and uppercase variations for better compatibility with database exports.

For CSV files, returns a list of dictionaries using csv.DictReader where each row
becomes a dictionary with column headers as keys. Note that CSV values are always
strings, unlike JSON which preserves data types.

- **Parameters**: - **fixtures_path** (*Union**[**Path**,**AsyncPath**]*) – The path to look for fixtures. Can be a `pathlib.Path` or
`anyio.Path` instance.
- **fixture_name** (*str*) – The fixture name to load (without file extension).
- **Raises**: - **FileNotFoundError** – If no fixture file is found with any supported extension.
- **OSError** – If there’s an error reading or decompressing the file.
- **ValueError** – If the JSON content is invalid, or if a zip file doesn’t contain
 the expected JSON/CSV files.
- **zipfile.BadZipFile** – If the zip file is corrupted.
- **gzip.BadGzipFile** – If the gzip file is corrupted.
- **csv.Error** – If the CSV content is malformed.
- **Returns**: The parsed data from the fixture file (JSON data or list of dictionaries from CSV).
- **Return type**: *Any*

> **Examples**: # Load JSON fixture
> >>> data = open_fixture(fixtures_path, “users”)
> # loads users.json, users.json.gz, or users.json.zip
> >>> print(data)
> [{“id”: 1, “name”: “Alice”}, {“id”: 2, “name”: “Bob”}]
>
> # Load CSV fixture
> >>> data = open_fixture(fixtures_path, “states”)
> # loads states.csv, states.csv.gz, or states.csv.zip
> >>> print(data)
> [{“abbreviation”: “AL”, “name”: “Alabama”}, {“abbreviation”: “AK”, “name”: “Alaska”}]

### `advanced_alchemy.utils.fixtures.open_fixture_async`

```python
async advanced_alchemy.utils.fixtures.open_fixture_async(fixtures_path, fixture_name)[source]
```

Loads JSON or CSV file with the specified fixture name asynchronously.

Supports plain files, gzipped files (.json.gz, .csv.gz), and zipped files (.json.zip, .csv.zip).
The function automatically detects the file format based on file extension and handles
decompression transparently. JSON files take priority over CSV files. Supports both
lowercase and uppercase variations for better compatibility with database exports.
For compressed files and CSV parsing, operations are performed in a thread pool to
avoid blocking the event loop.

For CSV files, returns a list of dictionaries using csv.DictReader where each row
becomes a dictionary with column headers as keys. Note that CSV values are always
strings, unlike JSON which preserves data types.

- **Parameters**: - **fixtures_path** (*Union**[**Path**,**AsyncPath**]*) – The path to look for fixtures. Can be a `pathlib.Path` or
`anyio.Path` instance.
- **fixture_name** (*str*) – The fixture name to load (without file extension).
- **Raises**: - [**MissingDependencyError**](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.MissingDependencyError) – If the `anyio` library is not installed.
- **FileNotFoundError** – If no fixture file is found with any supported extension.
- **OSError** – If there’s an error reading or decompressing the file.
- **ValueError** – If the JSON content is invalid, or if a zip file doesn’t contain
 the expected JSON/CSV files.
- **zipfile.BadZipFile** – If the zip file is corrupted.
- **gzip.BadGzipFile** – If the gzip file is corrupted.
- **csv.Error** – If the CSV content is malformed.
- **Returns**: The parsed data from the fixture file (JSON data or list of dictionaries from CSV).
- **Return type**: *Any*

> **Examples**: # Load JSON fixture
> >>> data = await open_fixture_async(fixtures_path, “users”)
> # loads users.json, users.json.gz, or users.json.zip
> >>> print(data)
> [{“id”: 1, “name”: “Alice”}, {“id”: 2, “name”: “Bob”}]
>
> # Load CSV fixture
> >>> data = await open_fixture_async(fixtures_path, “states”)
> # loads states.csv, states.csv.gz, or states.csv.zip
> >>> print(data)
> [{“abbreviation”: “AL”, “name”: “Alabama”}, {“abbreviation”: “AK”, “name”: “Alaska”}]

### `advanced_alchemy.utils.text.slugify`

```python
advanced_alchemy.utils.text.slugify(value, allow_unicode=False, separator=None)[source]
```

Slugify.

Convert to ASCII if `allow_unicode` is `False`. Convert spaces or repeated
dashes to single dashes. Remove characters that aren’t alphanumerics,
underscores, or hyphens. Convert to lowercase. Also strip leading and
trailing whitespace, dashes, and underscores.

- **Parameters**: - **value** (*str*) – the string to slugify
- **allow_unicode** (*bool*) – allow unicode characters in slug. Defaults to `False`.
- **separator** (*str**|**None*) – by default a `-` is used to delimit word boundaries.
Set this to configure something different.
- **Returns**: a slugified string of the value parameter
- **Return type**: *str*

### `advanced_alchemy.utils.text.check_email`

```python
advanced_alchemy.utils.text.check_email(email)[source]
```

Validate an email.

Very simple email validation.

- **Returns**: The validated email.

### `advanced_alchemy.utils.deprecation.deprecated`

```python
advanced_alchemy.utils.deprecation.deprecated(version, *, removal_in=None, alternative=None, info=None, pending=False, kind=None)[source]
```

Create a decorator wrapping a function, method or property with a warning call about a (pending) deprecation.

- **Parameters**: - **version** (*str*) – Advanced Alchemy version where the deprecation will occur
- **removal_in** (*str**|**None*) – Advanced Alchemy version where the deprecated function will be removed
- **alternative** (*str**|**None*) – Name of a function that should be used instead
- **info** (*str**|**None*) – Additional information
- **pending** (*bool*) – Use `PendingDeprecationWarning` instead of `DeprecationWarning`
- **kind** (*'function'**|**'method'**|**'classmethod'**|**'property'**|**None*) – Type of the deprecated callable. If `None`, will use `inspect` to figure
out if it’s a function or method
- **Returns**: A decorator wrapping the function call with a warning
- **Return type**: *Callable*[[*Callable*[[~P], *T*]], *Callable*[[~P], *T*]]

- **deprecated_name** (*str*) – Name of the deprecated function
- **removal_in** (*str**|**None*) – Advanced Alchemy version where the deprecated function will be removed
- **alternative** (*str**|**None*) – Name of a function that should be used instead

- **kind** (*'function'**|**'method'**|**'classmethod'**|**'attribute'**|**'property'**|**'class'**|**'parameter'**|**'import'*) – Type of the deprecated thing

```python
class advanced_alchemy.repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository(*, statement=None, session, auto_expunge=False, auto_refresh=True, auto_commit=False, order_by=None, error_messages=Empty, load=None, execution_options=None, wrap_exceptions=True, uniquify=None, count_with_window_function=None, cache_manager=None, bind_group=None, **kwargs)
```

Bases: [`SQLAlchemyAsyncRepositoryProtocol`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepositoryProtocol)␀ [[`ModelT`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.ModelT)], [`FilterableRepository`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.FilterableRepository)␀ [[`ModelT`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.ModelT)]

##### `delete`

```python
async delete(item_id, *, auto_commit=None, auto_expunge=None, id_attribute=None, error_messages=Empty, load=None, execution_options=None, uniquify=None, bind_group=None)
```

Delete instance identified by `item_id`.

- **Parameters**: - **item_id** (*Any**|**tuple**[**Any**,**...**]**|**dict**[**str**,**Any**]*) – Identifier of instance to be deleted. For single primary keys,
pass a scalar value. For composite primary keys, pass a tuple of values
in column order or a dict mapping attribute names to values.
- **auto_expunge** (*bool**|**None*) – Remove object from session before returning.
- **auto_commit** (*bool**|**None*) – Commit objects before returning.
- **id_attribute** (*str**|**InstrumentedAttribute**[**Any**]**|**None*) – Allows customization of the unique identifier to use for model fetching.
Defaults to `id`, but can reference any surrogate or candidate key for the table.
Note: Only applies to single-column lookups.
- **error_messages** ([*ErrorMessages*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.ErrorMessages)*|**type**[*[*Empty*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)*]**|**None*) – An optional dictionary of templates to use
for friendlier error messages to clients
- **load** ([*LoadSpec*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.LoadSpec)*|**None*) – Set default relationships to be loaded
- **execution_options** (*dict**[**str**,**Any**]**|**None*) – Set default execution options
- **uniquify** (*bool**|**None*) – Optionally apply the `unique()` method to results before returning.
- **bind_group** (*str**|**None*) – Optional routing group for multi-master configurations.
- **Returns**: The deleted instance.
- **Return type**: [*ModelT*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.ModelT)

> **Examples**: # Single primary key
> >>> deleted = await user_repo.delete(123)
>
> # Composite primary key
> >>> deleted = await user_role_repo.delete((user_id, role_id))

##### `get`

```python
async get(item_id, *, auto_expunge=None, statement=None, id_attribute=None, error_messages=Empty, load=None, execution_options=None, uniquify=None, with_for_update=None, use_cache=True, bind_group=None)
```

Get instance identified by `item_id`.

- **Parameters**: - **item_id** (*Any**|**tuple**[**Any**,**...**]**|**dict**[**str**,**Any**]*) – Identifier of the instance to be retrieved. For single primary keys,
pass a scalar value (int, str, UUID, etc.). For composite primary keys,
pass a tuple of values in column order or a dict mapping attribute names to values.
- **auto_expunge** (*bool**|**None*) – Remove object from session before returning.
- **statement** (*Select**|**None*) – To facilitate customization of the underlying select query.
- **id_attribute** (*str**|**InstrumentedAttribute**[**Any**]**|**None*) – Allows customization of the unique identifier to use for model fetching.
Defaults to `id`, but can reference any surrogate or candidate key for the table.
Note: Only applies to single-column lookups. For composite primary keys,
this parameter is ignored and the primary key columns are used automatically.
- **error_messages** ([*ErrorMessages*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.ErrorMessages)*|**type**[*[*Empty*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)*]**|**None*) – An optional dictionary of templates to use
for friendlier error messages to clients
- **load** ([*LoadSpec*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.LoadSpec)*|**None*) – Set relationships to be loaded
- **execution_options** (*dict**[**str**,**Any**]**|**None*) – Set default execution options
- **uniquify** (*bool**|**None*) – Optionally apply the `unique()` method to results before returning.
- **with_for_update** (*TypeAliasForwardRef**(**'sqlalchemy.sql.selectable.ForUpdateArg'**)**|**None**|**bool**|**Dict**[**str**,**Any**]*) – Optional FOR UPDATE clause / parameters to apply to the SELECT statement.
- **use_cache** (*bool*) – Whether to use caching for this query (default True).
- **bind_group** (*str**|**None*) – Optional routing group to use for the operation.
- **Returns**: The retrieved instance.
- **Return type**: [*ModelT*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.ModelT)

> **Examples**: # Single primary key
> >>> user = await user_repo.get(123)
>
> # Composite primary key (tuple format)
> >>> assignment = await user_role_repo.get((user_id, role_id))
>
> # Composite primary key (dict format)
> >>> assignment = await user_role_repo.get(
> … {
> … “user_id”: 1,
> … “role_id”: 5,
> … }
> … )

- **Raises**: - [**NotFoundError**](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.NotFoundError) – If no instance is found with the given primary key.
- **ValueError** – If the input format doesn’t match the primary key structure.
- **Return type**: [*ModelT*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.ModelT)

## Helpers & Type Definitions

### `advanced_alchemy.repository.get_instrumented_attr`

```python
advanced_alchemy.repository.get_instrumented_attr(model, key)
```

Get an instrumented attribute from a model.

- **Parameters**: - **model** (*type**[*[*ModelProtocol*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/base.html#advanced_alchemy.base.ModelProtocol)*]*) – SQLAlchemy model class.
- **key** (*str**|**InstrumentedAttribute**[**Any**]*) – Either a string attribute name or an `sqlalchemy.orm.InstrumentedAttribute`.
- **Returns**: The instrumented attribute from the model.
- **Return type**: `sqlalchemy.orm.InstrumentedAttribute`

### `advanced_alchemy.repository.model_from_dict`

```python
advanced_alchemy.repository.model_from_dict(model, /, **kwargs)
```

Create an ORM model instance from a dictionary of attributes.

This function recursively converts nested dictionaries into their
corresponding SQLAlchemy model instances for relationship attributes.

- **Parameters**: - **model** (*type**[*[*ModelT*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.ModelT)*]*) – The SQLAlchemy model class to instantiate.
- ****kwargs** (*Any*) – Keyword arguments containing model attribute values.
For relationship attributes, values can be:
- None: Sets the relationship to None
- dict: Recursively converted to the related model instance
- list[dict]: Each dict converted to related model instances
- Model instance: Passed through unchanged
- **Returns**: A new instance of the model populated with the provided values.
- **Return type**: [*ModelT*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.ModelT)

> **Example**: Basic usage with nested relationships:
>
> ```default
> data = {
>     "name": "John Doe",
>     "profile": {"bio": "Developer"},
>     "addresses": [
>         {"street": "123 Main St"},
>         {"street": "456 Oak Ave"},
>     ],
> }
> user = model_from_dict(User, **data)
> # user.profile is a Profile instance
> # user.addresses is a list of Address instances
> ```


Default error message templates mapped by exception category.

### `advanced_alchemy.repository.OrderingPair`

```python
advanced_alchemy.repository.OrderingPair
```

Type alias for ordering pairs.

A tuple of (column, ascending) where:
- column: Union[str, `sqlalchemy.orm.InstrumentedAttribute`]
- ascending: bool
- or a `sqlalchemy.sql.elements.UnaryExpression` which is the standard way to express an ordering in SQLAlchemy

This type is used to specify ordering criteria for repository queries.

Source: https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository_memory.html
