# filters

## Base & Pagination Filters

### `advanced_alchemy.filters.StatementFilter`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.filters.StatementFilter[source]
```

Bases: `ABC`

Abstract base class for SQLAlchemy statement filters.

This class defines the interface for all filter types in the system. Each filter
implementation must provide a method to append its filtering logic to an existing
SQLAlchemy statement.

##### `append_to_statement`

```python
abstractmethod append_to_statement(statement, model, *args, **kwargs)[source]
```

Append filter conditions to a SQLAlchemy statement.

- **Parameters**: - **statement** ([*StatementTypeT*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.StatementTypeT)) – The SQLAlchemy statement to modify
- **model** (*type**[**ModelT**]*) – The SQLAlchemy model class
- ***args** (*Any*) – Additional positional arguments
- ****kwargs** (*Any*) – Additional keyword arguments
- **Returns**: Modified SQLAlchemy statement with filter conditions applied
- **Return type**: [*StatementTypeT*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.StatementTypeT)
- **Raises**: **NotImplementedError** – If the concrete class doesn’t implement this method

> **Note**: This method must be implemented by all concrete filter classes.

> **See Also**: `sqlalchemy.sql.expression.Select.where()`: SQLAlchemy where clause

### `advanced_alchemy.filters.PaginationFilter`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.filters.PaginationFilter[source]
```

Bases: [`StatementFilter`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.StatementFilter), `ABC`

Abstract base class for pagination filters.

Subclasses should implement pagination logic, such as limit/offset or
cursor-based pagination.

##### `append_to_statement`

```python
abstractmethod append_to_statement(statement, model, *args, **kwargs)
```

Append filter conditions to a SQLAlchemy statement.

- **Parameters**: - **statement** ([*StatementTypeT*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.StatementTypeT)) – The SQLAlchemy statement to modify
- **model** (*type**[**ModelT**]*) – The SQLAlchemy model class
- ***args** (*Any*) – Additional positional arguments
- ****kwargs** (*Any*) – Additional keyword arguments
- **Returns**: Modified SQLAlchemy statement with filter conditions applied
- **Return type**: [*StatementTypeT*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.StatementTypeT)
- **Raises**: **NotImplementedError** – If the concrete class doesn’t implement this method

> **Note**: This method must be implemented by all concrete filter classes.

> **See Also**: `sqlalchemy.sql.expression.Select.where()`: SQLAlchemy where clause

### `advanced_alchemy.filters.LimitOffset`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.filters.LimitOffset(limit, offset)[source]
```

Bases: [`PaginationFilter`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.PaginationFilter)

Limit and offset pagination filter.

Implements traditional pagination using SQL LIMIT and OFFSET clauses.
Only applies to SELECT statements; other statement types are returned unmodified.

> **Note**: This filter only modifies SELECT statements. For other statement types
> (UPDATE, DELETE), the statement is returned unchanged.

> **See Also**: - `sqlalchemy.sql.expression.Select.limit()`: SQLAlchemy LIMIT clause
> - `sqlalchemy.sql.expression.Select.offset()`: SQLAlchemy OFFSET clause

### `advanced_alchemy.filters.OrderBy`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.filters.OrderBy(field_name, sort_order='asc', nulls=None)[source]
```

Bases: [`StatementFilter`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.StatementFilter)

Order by a specific field.

Appends an ORDER BY clause to SELECT statements, sorting records by the
specified field in ascending or descending order.

> **Note**: This filter only modifies SELECT statements. For other statement types,
> the statement is returned unchanged.

> **Note**: `nulls` controls where NULLs land. Left as `None` the database decides, and the
> databases disagree: PostgreSQL and Oracle sort NULLs last ascending and first descending,
> while MySQL and SQLite do the opposite. Set it explicitly for a stable order across
> backends — `nulls="last"` is usually what a user reading a descending list expects, since
> rows with no value otherwise fill the first page.
>
> MySQL, MariaDB and SQL Server have no `NULLS FIRST`/`NULLS LAST` syntax. They sort
> NULL as the lowest value, so `asc` with `nulls="first"` and `desc` with
> `nulls="last"` compile to the plain ordering term. The other two placements are emulated
> with a leading `CASE WHEN ... IS NULL` sort key. SQL Server requires every ORDER BY term
> to appear in the select list under `SELECT DISTINCT`, so combine `nulls` with a
> `DISTINCT` statement there only for those two native placements.

> **See Also**: - `sqlalchemy.sql.expression.Select.order_by()`: SQLAlchemy ORDER BY clause
> - `sqlalchemy.sql.expression.ColumnElement.asc()`: Ascending order
> - `sqlalchemy.sql.expression.ColumnElement.desc()`: Descending order
> - `sqlalchemy.sql.expression.nulls_first()`: NULLS FIRST
> - `sqlalchemy.sql.expression.nulls_last()`: NULLS LAST

## Date, Time & Nullability Filters

### `advanced_alchemy.filters.NullFilter`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.filters.NullFilter(field_name)[source]
```

Bases: [`StatementFilter`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.StatementFilter)

Filter for NULL values (IS NULL).

This filter creates IS NULL conditions for database fields.
Use this to find records where a field has no value.

> **Example**: Basic NULL filtering:
>
> ```default
> from advanced_alchemy.filters import NullFilter
>
> null_filter = NullFilter("email_verified_at")
> unverified = await repo.get_many(null_filter)
> ```
>
> With multiple filters:
>
> ```default
> from advanced_alchemy.filters import (
>     NullFilter,
>     CollectionFilter,
> )
>
> filters = [
>     NullFilter("email_verified_at"),
>     CollectionFilter("role", ["admin", "moderator"]),
> ]
> results = await repo.get_many(*filters)
> ```

> **See Also**: - [`NotNullFilter`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.NotNullFilter): Filter for NOT NULL values
> - [`CollectionFilter`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.CollectionFilter): Filter by collection membership
> - `sqlalchemy.sql.expression.ColumnOperators.is_()`: IS NULL operator

## Collection, Search & Comparison Filters

### `advanced_alchemy.filters.CollectionFilter`

This filter restricts records based on a field’s presence in a collection of values.

The filter supports both `IN` and `ANY` operators for collection membership testing.

### `advanced_alchemy.filters.SearchFilter`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.filters.SearchFilter(field_name, value, ignore_case=False, escape_wildcards=False)[source]
```

Bases: [`StatementFilter`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.StatementFilter)

Case-sensitive or case-insensitive substring matching filter.

Implements text search using SQL LIKE or ILIKE operators. Can search across
multiple fields using OR conditions.

> **Note**: The search pattern automatically adds wildcards before and after the search
> value, equivalent to SQL pattern ‘%value%’.

> **Note**: `%` and `_` in `value` remain SQL wildcards by default. Set
> `escape_wildcards=True` to match them literally on databases supporting
> the SQL `ESCAPE` clause. Spanner has no `ESCAPE` clause, so
> `escape_wildcards` must stay `False` there.

> **See Also**: - [`NotInSearchFilter`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.NotInSearchFilter): Opposite filter using NOT LIKE/ILIKE
> - `sqlalchemy.sql.expression.ColumnOperators.like()`: Case-sensitive LIKE
> - `sqlalchemy.sql.expression.ColumnOperators.ilike()`: Case-insensitive LIKE

### `advanced_alchemy.filters.NotInSearchFilter`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.filters.NotInSearchFilter(field_name, value, ignore_case=False, escape_wildcards=False)[source]
```

Bases: [`SearchFilter`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.SearchFilter)

Filter for excluding records that match a substring.

Implements negative text search using SQL NOT LIKE or NOT ILIKE operators.
Can exclude across multiple fields using AND conditions.

- **Parameters**: - **field_name** (*str**|*[*set*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/base.html#advanced_alchemy.base.MetadataRegistry.set)*[**str**]*) – Name or set of names of model attributes to search on
- **value** (*str*) – Text to exclude from the field(s)
- **ignore_case** (*bool**|**None*) – If True, uses NOT ILIKE for case-insensitive matching
- **escape_wildcards** (*bool*) – If True, matches wildcard characters literally using
SQL ESCAPE. Defaults to False; not supported by Spanner when enabled.

> **Note**: Uses AND for multiple fields, meaning records matching any field will be excluded.

> **See Also**: - [`SearchFilter`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.SearchFilter): Opposite filter using LIKE/ILIKE
> - `sqlalchemy.sql.expression.ColumnOperators.notlike()`: NOT LIKE operator
> - `sqlalchemy.sql.expression.ColumnOperators.notilike()`: NOT ILIKE operator

### `advanced_alchemy.filters.ComparisonFilter`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.filters.ComparisonFilter(field_name, operator, value)[source]
```

Bases: [`StatementFilter`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.StatementFilter)

Simple comparison filter for equality and inequality operations.

This filter applies basic comparison operators (=, !=, >, >=, <, <=) to a field.
It provides a generic way to perform common comparison operations.

- **Parameters**: - **field_name** (*Any*) – Name of the model attribute to filter on
- **operator** (*str*) – Comparison operator to use (must be one of: ‘eq’, ‘ne’, ‘gt’, ‘ge’, ‘lt’, ‘le’, ‘in’, ‘notin’, ‘between’, ‘like’, ‘ilike’, ‘startswith’, ‘istartswith’, ‘endswith’, ‘iendswith’, ‘dateeq’)
- **value** (*Any*) – Value to compare against
- **Raises**: **ValueError** – If an invalid operator is provided

### `advanced_alchemy.filters.ExistsFilter`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.filters.ExistsFilter(values, operator='and')[source]
```

Bases: [`StatementFilter`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.StatementFilter)

Filter for EXISTS subqueries.

This filter creates an EXISTS condition using a list of column expressions.
The expressions can be combined using either AND or OR logic.

> **Important**: `values` must include the condition that joins the subquery to the outer query.
> `correlate()` only *permits* correlation; it cannot
> infer a join. Conditions that never mention the outer table produce a standalone subquery,
> which is true whenever any row matches it — so the filter matches **every** row of the outer
> query rather than raising.

- **Parameters**: - **values** ([*list*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository.list)*[**ColumnElement**[**bool**]**]*) – List of SQLAlchemy column expressions to use in the EXISTS clause, including the
correlation between the outer table and the subquery table.
- **operator** (*'and'**|**'or'*) – If “and”, combines conditions with AND, otherwise uses OR. Defaults to “and”.

> **Example**: Basic usage with AND conditions:
>
> ```default
> from sqlalchemy import select
> from advanced_alchemy.filters import ExistsFilter
>
> filter = ExistsFilter(
>     values=[
>         User.organization_id == Organization.id,
>         User.email.like("%@example.com%"),
>     ],
> )
> statement = filter.append_to_statement(
>     select(Organization), Organization
> )
> ```
>
> This will return only organizations that have a user whose email contains “@example.com”.
>
> Using OR conditions:
>
> ```default
> filter = ExistsFilter(
>     values=[User.role == "admin", User.role == "owner"],
>     operator="or",
> )
> ```
>
> Note that this example is *not* correlated on its own — combine it with the correlation, or
> nest it in a [`FilterGroup`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.FilterGroup), to restrict the outer query.

> **See Also**: - [`NotExistsFilter`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.NotExistsFilter): The inverse of this filter
> - `sqlalchemy.sql.expression.exists()`: SQLAlchemy EXISTS expression

### `advanced_alchemy.filters.NotExistsFilter`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.filters.NotExistsFilter(values, operator='and')[source]
```

Bases: [`StatementFilter`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.StatementFilter)

Filter for NOT EXISTS subqueries.

This filter creates a NOT EXISTS condition using a list of column expressions.
The expressions can be combined using either AND or OR logic. The filter applies
a correlated subquery that returns only the rows from the main query that DO NOT
match the specified conditions.

For example, if searching movies with `Movie.genre == “Action”`, only rows where
the genre is NOT “Action” will be returned.

- **Parameters**: - **values** ([*list*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository.list)*[**ColumnElement**[**bool**]**]*) – List of SQLAlchemy column expressions to use in the NOT EXISTS clause.
- **operator** (*'and'**|**'or'*) – If “and”, combines conditions with AND, otherwise uses OR. Defaults to “and”.

> **Example**: Basic usage with AND conditions:
>
> ```default
> from sqlalchemy import select
> from advanced_alchemy.filters import NotExistsFilter
>
> filter = NotExistsFilter(
>     values=[User.email.like("%@example.com%")],
> )
> statement = filter.append_to_statement(
>     select(Organization), Organization
> )
> ```
>
> This will return only organizations where the user’s email does NOT contain “@example.com”.
>
> Using OR conditions:
>
> ```default
> filter = NotExistsFilter(
>     values=[User.role == "admin", User.role == "owner"],
>     operator="or",
> )
> ```
>
> This will return organizations where the user’s role is NEITHER “admin” NOR “owner”.

> **See Also**: - [`ExistsFilter`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.ExistsFilter): The inverse of this filter
> - `sqlalchemy.sql.expression.not_()`: SQLAlchemy NOT operator
> - `sqlalchemy.sql.expression.exists()`: SQLAlchemy EXISTS expression

### `advanced_alchemy.service.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepositoryReadService`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.service.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepositoryReadService(session, *, statement=None, auto_expunge=False, auto_refresh=True, auto_commit=False, order_by=None, error_messages=Empty, wrap_exceptions=True, load=None, execution_options=None, uniquify=None, count_with_window_function=None, **repo_kwargs)
```

Bases: [`ResultConverter`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/service.html#advanced_alchemy.service.ResultConverter), `Generic`␀ [[`ModelT`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.ModelT), `SQLAlchemyAsyncRepositoryT`]

Service object that operates on a repository object.

repository_type: type[SQLAlchemyAsyncRepositoryT]
```

Type of the repository to use.

##### `count`

```python
async count(*filters, statement=None, error_messages=Empty, load=None, execution_options=None, uniquify=None, bind_group=None, **kwargs)
```

Count of records returned by query.

- **Parameters**: - ***filters** ([*StatementFilter*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.StatementFilter)*|**ColumnElement**[**bool**]*) – arguments for filtering.
- **statement** (*Select**|**None*) – To facilitate customization of the underlying select query.
- **error_messages** ([*ErrorMessages*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.ErrorMessages)*|**type**[*[*Empty*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)*]**|**None*) – An optional dictionary of templates to use
for friendlier error messages to clients
- **load** ([*LoadSpec*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.LoadSpec)*|**None*) – Set relationships to be loaded
- **execution_options** (*dict**[**str**,**Any**]**|**None*) – Set default execution options
- **uniquify** (*bool**|**None*) – Optionally apply the `unique()` method to results before returning.
- **bind_group** (*str**|**None*) – The bind group to use for the operation.
- ****kwargs** (*Any*) – key value pairs of filter types.
- **Returns**: A count of the collection, filtered, but ignoring pagination.
- **Return type**: *int*

##### `get`

```python
async get(item_id, *, statement=None, id_attribute=None, auto_expunge=None, error_messages=Empty, load=None, execution_options=None, uniquify=None, bind_group=None)
```

Wrap repository scalar operation.

- **Parameters**: - **item_id** (*Any**|**tuple**[**Any**,**...**]**|**dict**[**str**,**Any**]*) – Identifier of instance to be retrieved.
For single primary key models, pass a scalar value (int, str, UUID, etc.).
For composite primary key models, pass a tuple of values in column order,
or a dict mapping attribute names to values.
- **auto_expunge** (*bool**|**None*) – Remove object from session before returning.
- **statement** (*Select**|**None*) – To facilitate customization of the underlying select query.
- **id_attribute** (*str**|**InstrumentedAttribute**[**Any**]**|**None*) – Allows customization of the unique identifier to use for model fetching.
Defaults to `id`, but can reference any surrogate or candidate key for the table.
Only applicable for single primary key models.
- **error_messages** ([*ErrorMessages*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.ErrorMessages)*|**type**[*[*Empty*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)*]**|**None*) – An optional dictionary of templates to use
for friendlier error messages to clients
- **load** ([*LoadSpec*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.LoadSpec)*|**None*) – Set relationships to be loaded
- **execution_options** (*dict**[**str**,**Any**]**|**None*) – Set default execution options
- **uniquify** (*bool**|**None*) – Optionally apply the `unique()` method to results before returning.
- **bind_group** (*str**|**None*) – The bind group to use for the operation.
- **Returns**: Representation of instance with identifier `item_id`.
- **Return type**: [*ModelT*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.ModelT)

> **Examples**: # Single primary key
> >>> user = await service.get(123)
>
> # Composite primary key (tuple format)
> >>> assignment = await service.get((user_id, role_id))
>
> # Composite primary key (dict format)
> >>> assignment = await service.get({“user_id”: 1, “role_id”: 5})

### `advanced_alchemy.service.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepositoryService`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.service.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepositoryService
```

##### `delete`

```python
async delete(item_id, *, auto_commit=None, auto_expunge=None, id_attribute=None, error_messages=Empty, load=None, execution_options=None, uniquify=None, bind_group=None)
```

Wrap repository delete operation.

- **Parameters**: - **item_id** (*Any**|**tuple**[**Any**,**...**]**|**dict**[**str**,**Any**]*) – Identifier of instance to be deleted.
For single primary key models, pass a scalar value (int, str, UUID, etc.).
For composite primary key models, pass a tuple of values in column order,
or a dict mapping attribute names to values.
- **auto_commit** (*bool**|**None*) – Commit objects before returning.
- **auto_expunge** (*bool**|**None*) – Remove object from session before returning.
- **id_attribute** (*str**|**InstrumentedAttribute**[**Any**]**|**None*) – Allows customization of the unique identifier to use for model fetching.
Defaults to `id`, but can reference any surrogate or candidate key for the table.
Only applicable for single primary key models.
- **error_messages** ([*ErrorMessages*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.ErrorMessages)*|**type**[*[*Empty*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.Empty)*]**|**None*) – An optional dictionary of templates to use
for friendlier error messages to clients
- **load** ([*LoadSpec*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.LoadSpec)*|**None*) – Set default relationships to be loaded
- **execution_options** (*dict**[**str**,**Any**]**|**None*) – Set default execution options
- **uniquify** (*bool**|**None*) – Optionally apply the `unique()` method to results before returning.
- **bind_group** (*str**|**None*) – Optional routing group to use for the operation.
- **Returns**: Representation of the deleted instance.
- **Return type**: [*ModelT*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.ModelT)

> **Examples**: # Single primary key
> >>> deleted_user = await service.delete(123)
>
> # Composite primary key (tuple format)
> >>> deleted = await service.delete((user_id, role_id))
>
> # Composite primary key (dict format)
> >>> deleted = await service.delete({“user_id”: 1, “role_id”: 5})

## Conversion, Pagination & Helpers

### `advanced_alchemy.service.ResultConverter`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.service.ResultConverter
```

Bases: `object`

Simple mixin to help convert to a paginated response model.

Single objects are transformed to the supplied schema type, and lists of objects are automatically transformed into an `OffsetPagination` response of the supplied schema type.

- **Parameters**: **data** – A database model instance or row mapping.
Type: [`ModelOrRowMappingT`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.ModelOrRowMappingT)
- **Returns**: The converted schema object.

##### `to_schema`

```python
to_schema(data, total=None, filters=None, *, schema_type=None)
```

Convert the object to a response schema.

When `schema_type` is None, the model is returned with no conversion.

- **Parameters**: - **data** (*Union**[*[*ModelOrRowMappingT*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.ModelOrRowMappingT)*,**Sequence**[*[*ModelOrRowMappingT*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.ModelOrRowMappingT)*]**,*[*ModelProtocol*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/base.html#advanced_alchemy.base.ModelProtocol)*,**Sequence**[*[*ModelProtocol*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/base.html#advanced_alchemy.base.ModelProtocol)*]**,**RowMapping**,**Sequence**[**RowMapping**]**,**Row**[**Any**]**,**Sequence**[**Row**[**Any**]**]**,**dict**[**str**,**Any**]**,**Sequence**[**dict**[**str**,**Any**]**]**]*) – The return from one of the service calls.
Type: [`ModelOrRowMappingT`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.ModelOrRowMappingT)
- **total** (*Optional**[**int**]*) – The total number of rows in the data.
- **filters** (*Union**[**Sequence**[**Union**[*[*StatementFilter*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.StatementFilter)*,**ColumnElement**[**bool**]**]**]**,**Sequence**[*[*StatementFilter*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.StatementFilter)*]**,**None**]*) – [`StatementFilter`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.StatementFilter) | `ColumnElement` collection of route filters.
- **schema_type** (*Optional**[**type**[*[*ModelDTOT*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/service.html#advanced_alchemy.service.ModelDTOT)*]**]*) – [`ModelDTOT`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/service.html#advanced_alchemy.service.ModelDTOT) Optional schema type to convert the data to
- **Raises**: [**AdvancedAlchemyError**](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.AdvancedAlchemyError) – If `schema_type` is not a valid Pydantic, Msgspec, or attrs schema and all libraries are not installed.

- **Return type**: *Union*[[*ModelOrRowMappingT*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.ModelOrRowMappingT), [*OffsetPagination*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/service.html#advanced_alchemy.service.OffsetPagination)[[*ModelOrRowMappingT*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.ModelOrRowMappingT)], [*ModelDTOT*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/service.html#advanced_alchemy.service.ModelDTOT), [*OffsetPagination*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/service.html#advanced_alchemy.service.OffsetPagination)[[*ModelDTOT*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/service.html#advanced_alchemy.service.ModelDTOT)]]

### `advanced_alchemy.service.fields`

```python
advanced_alchemy.service.fields(cls)
```

Return the tuple of *attrs* attributes for a class or instance.

The tuple also allows accessing the fields by their names (see below for
examples).

- **Parameters**: **cls** (`type`) – Class or instance to introspect.
- **Raises**: - **TypeError** – If *cls* is neither a class nor an *attrs* instance.
- **attrs.exceptions.NotAnAttrsClassError** – If *cls* is not an *attrs* class.
- **Returns**: tuple (with name accessors) of `attrs.Attribute`

> **Versionmodified**: Changed in version 16.2.0: Returned tuple allows accessing the fields
> by name.

> **Versionmodified**: Changed in version 23.1.0: Add support for generic classes.

> **Versionmodified**: Changed in version 26.1.0: Add support for instances.

that will be decoded using the given encoding and error handler.
Otherwise, returns the result of object.__str__() (if defined)
or repr(object).
encoding defaults to ‘utf-8’.
errors defaults to ‘strict’.

Source: https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/routing.html

# routing

Read/write replica session routing for SQLAlchemy engines and sessions. See
[`RoutingConfig`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/config/routing.html#advanced_alchemy.config.routing.RoutingConfig),
[`ReplicaConfig`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/config/routing.html#advanced_alchemy.config.routing.ReplicaConfig), and
[`RoutingStrategy`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/config/routing.html#advanced_alchemy.config.routing.RoutingStrategy) for configuration.

## Routing Sessions & Session Makers

### `advanced_alchemy.routing.RoutingAsyncSession`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.routing.RoutingAsyncSession(routing_config, selectors, default_engine, **kwargs)
```

Bases: `AsyncSession`

Async session with read/write routing support.

Wraps [`RoutingSyncSession`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/routing.html#advanced_alchemy.routing.RoutingSyncSession) to provide async routing capabilities.

### `advanced_alchemy.routing.RoutingSyncSession`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.routing.RoutingSyncSession(routing_config, selectors, default_engine, **kwargs)
```

Bases: `Session`

Synchronous session with read/write routing via `get_bind()`.

This session class extends SQLAlchemy’s `Session` to provide
automatic routing of operations to different engine groups (e.g. writer/reader).

The routing decision is made in `get_bind()` based on:
1. Execution options (`bind_group`)
2. Context variables (`bind_group`, `force_primary`)
3. Stickiness state
4. Operation type (Write vs Read)

- **Variables**: - **_default_engine** (*Engine*) – The default (write) database engine.
- **_selectors** (*dict**[**str**,*[*EngineSelector*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/routing.html#advanced_alchemy.routing.selectors.EngineSelector)*[**Engine**]**]*) – Map of group names to engine selectors.
- **_routing_config** ([*RoutingConfig*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/config/routing.html#advanced_alchemy.config.routing.RoutingConfig)) – Configuration for routing behavior.

##### `get_bind`

```python
get_bind(mapper=None, clause=None, **kwargs)
```

Route to appropriate engine based on operation and context.

- **Parameters**: - **mapper** (*Mapper**[**Any**]**|**type**[**Any**]**|**None*) – Optional mapper for the operation.
- **clause** (*Any**|**None*) – The SQL clause being executed.
- ****kwargs** (*Any*) – Additional keyword arguments.
- **Returns**: The selected engine.
- **Return type**: Engine

### `advanced_alchemy.routing.RoutingAsyncSessionMaker`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.routing.RoutingAsyncSessionMaker(routing_config, engine_config=None, session_config=None, create_engine_callable=create_async_engine)
```

Bases: `object`

Factory for creating async routing sessions.

This class creates [`RoutingAsyncSession`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/routing.html#advanced_alchemy.routing.RoutingAsyncSession) instances with properly
configured async engines and routing selectors.

> **Example**: Creating an async routing session maker:
>
> ```default
> maker = RoutingAsyncSessionMaker(
>     routing_config=RoutingConfig(
>         engines={
>             "writer": ["postgresql+asyncpg://primary"],
>             "reader": ["postgresql+asyncpg://replica1"],
>         }
>     ),
>     engine_config={"pool_size": 10},
> )
>
> async with maker() as session:
>     result = await session.execute(select(User))
> ```

##### `close_all`

```python
async close_all()
```

Close all engines and release connections.

Call this when shutting down to properly release database connections.

### `advanced_alchemy.routing.RoutingSyncSessionMaker`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.routing.RoutingSyncSessionMaker(routing_config, engine_config=None, session_config=None, create_engine_callable=create_engine)
```

Bases: `object`

Factory for creating sync routing sessions.

This class creates [`RoutingSyncSession`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/routing.html#advanced_alchemy.routing.RoutingSyncSession) instances with properly
configured engines and routing selectors.

> **Example**: Creating a routing session maker:
>
> ```default
> maker = RoutingSyncSessionMaker(
>     routing_config=RoutingConfig(
>         engines={
>             "writer": ["postgresql://primary"],
>             "reader": ["postgresql://replica1"],
>         }
>     ),
>     engine_config={"pool_size": 10},
> )
>
> session = maker()
> ```

##### `close_all`

```python
close_all()
```

Close all engines and release connections.

Call this when shutting down to properly release database connections.

### `advanced_alchemy.routing.dispose_session_maker_async`

```python
async advanced_alchemy.routing.dispose_session_maker_async(session_maker)
```

Dispose all engines owned by an async routing session maker.

No-op for non-routing session makers; the framework is responsible for
disposing `engine_instance` separately. Use during application shutdown
to release connections held by routing pools (primary + replicas).

- **Parameters**: **session_maker** (*Any*) – A session maker instance (any type).

### `advanced_alchemy.routing.dispose_session_maker_sync`

```python
advanced_alchemy.routing.dispose_session_maker_sync(session_maker)
```

Dispose all engines owned by a sync routing session maker.

No-op for non-routing session makers; the framework is responsible for
disposing `engine_instance` separately. Use during application shutdown
to release connections held by routing pools (primary + replicas).

- **Parameters**: **session_maker** (*Any*) – A session maker instance (any type).

## Replica Selectors

### `advanced_alchemy.routing.selectors.EngineSelector`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.routing.selectors.EngineSelector(engines)[source]
```

Bases: `ABC`, `Generic`␀ [`EngineT`]

Abstract base class for engine selection strategies.

Subclasses implement different algorithms for choosing which
engine to use for operations.

- **Variables**: **_engines** – List of engines to select from.

##### `next`

```python
abstractmethod next()[source]
```

Select the next engine to use.

- **Returns**: The selected engine.
- **Raises**: **RuntimeError** – If no engines are available.
- **Return type**: *EngineT*

#### `advanced_alchemy.routing.ReplicaSelector`

```python
advanced_alchemy.routing.ReplicaSelector
```

alias of [`EngineSelector`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/routing.html#advanced_alchemy.routing.selectors.EngineSelector)

### `advanced_alchemy.routing.RoundRobinSelector`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.routing.RoundRobinSelector(engines)
```

Bases: [`EngineSelector`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/routing.html#advanced_alchemy.routing.selectors.EngineSelector)␀ [`EngineT`]

Round-robin engine selection.

Cycles through engines in order, distributing load evenly
across all available engines.

This selector is thread-safe.

> **Example**: Creating a round-robin selector:
>
> ```default
> selector = RoundRobinSelector(engines)
> engine1 = selector.next()
> engine2 = selector.next()
> engine3 = selector.next()
> ```
>
> This cycles through engines in order and wraps back to the first.

##### `next`

```python
next()
```

Select the next engine in round-robin order.

- **Returns**: The next engine in the cycle.
- **Raises**: **RuntimeError** – If no engines are configured.
- **Return type**: *EngineT*

### `advanced_alchemy.routing.RandomSelector`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.routing.RandomSelector
```

Bases: [`EngineSelector`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/routing.html#advanced_alchemy.routing.selectors.EngineSelector)␀ [`EngineT`]

Random engine selection.

Selects engines randomly, which can help with load distribution
when engines have varying capacity or when you want to avoid
predictable patterns.

> **Example**: Creating a random selector:
>
> ```default
> selector = RandomSelector(engines)
> engine = selector.next()
> ```

##### `next`

```python
next()
```

Select a random engine.

- **Returns**: A randomly selected engine.
- **Raises**: **RuntimeError** – If no engines are configured.
- **Return type**: *EngineT*

## Routing Context Managers & State

### `advanced_alchemy.routing.primary_context`

```python
advanced_alchemy.routing.primary_context()
```

Force all operations to use primary within this context.

Use this context manager when you need to ensure all database operations
(including reads) go to the primary database.

> **Example**: Force a specific query to use the primary database:
>
> ```default
> from advanced_alchemy.routing import primary_context
>
> with primary_context():
>     user = await repo.get(user_id)
>     orders = await order_repo.get_many()
> ```

- **Yields**: None
- **Return type**: *Generator*[*None*, *None*, *None*]

### `advanced_alchemy.routing.replica_context`

```python
advanced_alchemy.routing.replica_context()
```

Force read operations to use replicas (temporarily disable stickiness).

Use this context manager when you want to explicitly allow reads to go
to replicas, even if a previous write has set the sticky-to-primary state.

> **Warning**: Use with caution! This can lead to read-after-write inconsistency
> if you’re reading data that was recently written.

> **Example**: Allow reads to use replicas after a write:
>
> ```default
> from advanced_alchemy.routing import replica_context
>
> await repo.add(user)
>
> user = await repo.get(user_id)
>
> with replica_context():
>     users = await repo.get_many()
> ```

- **Yields**: None
- **Return type**: *Generator*[*None*, *None*, *None*]

### `advanced_alchemy.routing.use_bind_group`

```python
advanced_alchemy.routing.use_bind_group(name)
```

Force operations to use a specific bind group.

Use this context manager to route operations to a specific group of engines,
such as “analytics” or “reporting”.

> **Example**: Route a query to the analytics database:
>
> ```default
> from advanced_alchemy.routing import use_bind_group
>
> with use_bind_group("analytics"):
>     data = await repo.get_many()
> ```

- **Parameters**: **name** (*str*) – Name of the bind group to use.
- **Yields**: None
- **Return type**: *Generator*[*None*, *None*, *None*]

### `advanced_alchemy.routing.reset_routing_context`

```python
advanced_alchemy.routing.reset_routing_context()
```

Reset all routing context variables to their defaults.

This is typically called after a commit or rollback to allow
subsequent reads to use replicas again.

> **Example**: Manual reset after transaction:
>
> ```default
> from advanced_alchemy.routing import reset_routing_context
>
> await session.commit()
> reset_routing_context()
> ```

### `advanced_alchemy.routing.stick_to_primary_var`

```python
advanced_alchemy.routing.stick_to_primary_var: contextvars.ContextVar[bool]
```

Context variable tracking whether subsequent reads should stick to the primary after a write.

### `advanced_alchemy.routing.force_primary_var`

```python
advanced_alchemy.routing.force_primary_var: contextvars.ContextVar[bool]
```

Context variable forcing operations onto the primary engine.

Source: https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/index.html

## Session Lifecycle Handlers

### `advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.async_autocommit_before_send_handler`

```python
async advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.async_autocommit_before_send_handler(message, scope)
```

Handle commit/rollback, closing and cleaning up sessions before sending.

- **Parameters**: - **message** (*Message*) – ASGI-`litestar.types.Message`
- **scope** (*Scope*) – An ASGI-`litestar.types.Scope`

### `advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.async_autocommit_handler_maker`

```python
advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.async_autocommit_handler_maker(commit_on_redirect=False, extra_commit_statuses=None, extra_rollback_statuses=None, session_scope_key=SESSION_SCOPE_KEY)
```

Set up the handler to issue a transaction commit or rollback based on specified status codes
:param commit_on_redirect: Issue a commit when the response status is a redirect (`3XX`)
:param extra_commit_statuses: A set of additional status codes that trigger a commit
:param extra_rollback_statuses: A set of additional status codes that trigger a rollback
:param session_scope_key: The key to use within the application state

- **Raises**: **ValueError** – If the extra commit statuses and extra rollback statuses share any status codes
- **Returns**: The handler callable
- **Return type**: *Callable*[[Message, Scope], *Coroutine*[*Any*, *Any*, *None*]]

advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.providers.create_service_dependencies(service_class, /, key, statement=None, config=None, error_messages=Empty, load=None, execution_options=None, filters=None, uniquify=None, count_with_window_function=None, dep_defaults=DEPENDENCY_DEFAULTS)[source]

Create a dependency provider for the combined filter function.

- **execution_options** (*Optional**[**dict**[**str**,**Any**]**]*) – The execution options to use for the service.

- **uniquify** (*bool**|**None*) – Whether to uniquify the service.
- **count_with_window_function** (*bool**|**None*) – Whether to count with a window function.
- **dep_defaults** ([*DependencyDefaults*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/fastapi/index.html#advanced_alchemy.extensions.fastapi.providers.DependencyDefaults)) – The dependency defaults to use for the service.
- **Returns**: A dictionary of dependency providers for the service.
- **Return type**: *dict*[*str*, *Provide*]

## DTO Factory & Configuration

class advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.dto.SQLAlchemyDTO[source]
```

Bases: `AbstractDTO`, `Generic`␀ [`T`]

Support for domain modelling with SQLAlchemy.

##### `config`

config: ClassVar[SQLAlchemyDTOConfig]
```

Config objects to define properties of the DTO.

##### `generate_field_definitions`

```python
classmethod generate_field_definitions(model_type)[source]
```

Generate DTO field definitions from a SQLAlchemy model.

- **Parameters**: **model_type** (*type**[**DeclarativeBase**]*) – The SQLAlchemy model type to generate field definitions from.
- **Yields**: A generator yielding DTO field definitions.
- **Raises**: **RuntimeError** – If the mapper cannot be found for the model type.
- **Return type**: *Generator*[*DTOFieldDefinition*, *None*, *None*]

- **Returns**: `True` if `field_definition` represents a nested model field.
- **Return type**: *bool*

### `advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.dto.SQLAlchemyDTOConfig`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.dto.SQLAlchemyDTOConfig(exclude=<factory>, include=<factory>, rename_fields=<factory>, rename_strategy=None, max_nested_depth=1, partial=False, underscore_fields_private=True, experimental_codegen_backend=None, forbid_unknown_fields=False, include_implicit_fields=True)[source]
```

Bases: `DTOConfig`

Additional controls for the generated SQLAlchemy DTO.

##### `exclude`

```python
exclude: Set[str | InstrumentedAttribute[Any]]
```

Explicitly exclude fields from the generated DTO.

If exclude is specified, all fields not specified in exclude will be included by default.

> **Notes**: - - **The field names are dot-separated paths to nested fields, e.g. `"address.street"` will**: exclude the `"street"` field from a nested `"address"` model.
> - - **‘exclude’ mutually exclusive with ‘include’ - specifying both values will raise an**: `ImproperlyConfiguredException`.

##### `include`

```python
include: Set[str | InstrumentedAttribute[Any]]
```

Explicitly include fields in the generated DTO.

If include is specified, all fields not specified in include will be excluded by default.

> **Notes**: - - **The field names are dot-separated paths to nested fields, e.g. `"address.street"` will**: include the `"street"` field from a nested `"address"` model.
> - - **‘include’ mutually exclusive with ‘exclude’ - specifying both values will raise an**: `ImproperlyConfiguredException`.

##### `rename_fields`

```python
rename_fields: dict[str | InstrumentedAttribute[Any], str]
```

Mapping of field names, to new name.

##### `include_implicit_fields`

```python
include_implicit_fields: bool | 'hybrid-only' = True
```

Fields that are implicitly mapped are included.

Turning this off will lead to exclude all fields not using `Mapped` annotation,

When setting this to `hybrid-only`, all implicitly mapped fields are excluded
with the exception for hybrid properties.

## DTO Type Helpers

### `advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.dto.parse_type_from_element`

```python
advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.dto.parse_type_from_element(elem, orm_descriptor)[source]
```

Parses a type from a SQLAlchemy element.

- **Parameters**: - **elem** (*Column**[**TypeAliasForwardRef**(**'typing.Any'**)**]**|**RelationshipProperty**[**TypeAliasForwardRef**(**'typing.Any'**)**]**|**CompositeProperty**[**TypeAliasForwardRef**(**'typing.Any'**)**]**|**ColumnClause**[**TypeAliasForwardRef**(**'typing.Any'**)**]**|**Label**[**TypeAliasForwardRef**(**'typing.Any'**)**]*) – The SQLAlchemy element to parse.
- **orm_descriptor** (*InspectionAttr*) – The attribute `elem` was extracted from.
- **Raises**: [**ImproperConfigurationError**](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.ImproperConfigurationError) – If the type cannot be parsed.
- **Returns**: The parsed type.
- **Return type**: FieldDefinition

### `advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.dto.detect_nullable_relationship`

```python
advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.dto.detect_nullable_relationship(elem)[source]
```

Detects if a relationship is nullable.

For MANYTOONE relationships (FK on this side), checks if all FK columns are nullable.
For ONETOMANY with uselist=False (inverse side of one-to-one), the related object may not
exist since no local FK enforces it, so these are always treated as nullable.

- **Parameters**: **elem** (*RelationshipProperty**[**Any**]*) – The relationship to check.
- **Returns**: `True` if the relationship is nullable, `False` otherwise.
- **Return type**: *bool*

Source: https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/litestar/session.html

Store `data` under the `session_id` for later retrieval.

If there is already data associated with `session_id`, replace
it with `data` and reset its expiry time

- **Parameters**: - **session_id** (*str*) – The session-ID.
- **data** (*bytes*) – Serialized session data
- **store** (*Store*) – The store to store the session in (not used in this backend)

- **Parameters**: - **session_id** (*str*) – The session-ID
- **store** (*Store*) – The store to delete the session from (not used in this backend)

Delete all session data.

# SQLAlchemy Store

This module provides a SQLAlchemy-backed implementation of Litestar’s
`Store` protocol. Register a
[`SQLAlchemyStore`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/litestar/store.html#advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.store.SQLAlchemyStore) under the `"sessions"` store name to back Litestar’s
server-side session middleware with your SQLAlchemy database. Invalid store or
model configuration raises `litestar.exceptions.ImproperlyConfiguredException`.

## Store Model Mixin

### `advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.store.StoreModelMixin`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.store.StoreModelMixin[source]

## Store Implementation

### `advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.store.SQLAlchemyStore`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.store.SQLAlchemyStore(config, model=StoreModelMixin, namespace=Empty)[source]
```

Bases: `NamespacedStore`, `Generic`␀ [`SQLAlchemyConfigT`]

SQLAlchemy based, thread and process safe asynchronous key/value store.

Supports both synchronous and asynchronous SQLAlchemy configurations.

##### `set`

```python
async set(key, value, expires_in=None)[source]
```

Set a value. Handles both sync and async backends.

##### `get`

```python
async get(key, renew_for=None)[source]
```

Get a value. Handles both sync and async backends.

- **Parameters**: - **key** (*str*) – The key to get the value for.
- **renew_for** (*int**|**timedelta**|**None*) – The amount of time to renew the value for.
- **Returns**: The value of the key, or None if the key does not exist or has expired.
- **Return type**: *bytes* | *None*

##### `delete`

```python
async delete(key)[source]
```

Delete a value. Handles both sync and async backends.

- **Parameters**: **key** (*str*) – The key to delete.

##### `delete_all`

```python
async delete_all()[source]
```

Delete all values in the namespace. Handles both sync and async backends.

- **Parameters**: **key** – The key to delete.

##### `delete_expired`

```python
async delete_expired()[source]
```

Delete expired values in this namespace using either a sync or async backend.

Values expiring at or before the current time are deleted. Values without an
expiration time and values in other namespaces are preserved. Call this method
periodically to reclaim storage; expired values are otherwise only hidden by reads.

- **Raises**: **ImproperlyConfiguredException** – If no namespace is configured.

##### `exists`

```python
async exists(key)[source]
```

Check if a key exists. Handles both sync and async backends.

- **Parameters**: **key** (*str*) – The key to check if it exists.
- **Returns**: True if the key exists, False otherwise.
- **Return type**: *bool*

##### `expires_in`

```python
async expires_in(key)[source]
```

Get expiration time. Handles both sync and async backends.

- **Parameters**: **key** (*str*) – The key to get the expiration time for.
- **Returns**: The expiration time in seconds, or None if the key does not exist or has no expiration time.
- **Return type**: *int* | *None*

##### `with_namespace`

```python
with_namespace(namespace)[source]
```

Return a new [`SQLAlchemyStore`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/litestar/store.html#advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.store.SQLAlchemyStore) with a nested virtual key namespace.

- **Return type**: [*SQLAlchemyStore*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/litestar/store.html#advanced_alchemy.extensions.litestar.store.SQLAlchemyStore)[*SQLAlchemyConfigT*]

Source: https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/litestar/cli.html

# FastAPI

API Reference for the `FastAPI` extensions module.

## Extension & CLI

### `advanced_alchemy.extensions.fastapi.AdvancedAlchemy`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.extensions.fastapi.AdvancedAlchemy(config, app=None)
```

Bases: [`AdvancedAlchemy`](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/starlette/index.html#advanced_alchemy.extensions.starlette.AdvancedAlchemy)

AdvancedAlchemy integration for FastAPI applications.

This class manages SQLAlchemy sessions and engine lifecycle within a FastAPI application.
It provides middleware for handling transactions based on commit strategies.

##### `provide_service`

```python
provide_service(service_class, /, key=None, statement=None, error_messages=Empty, load=None, execution_options=None, uniquify=None, count_with_window_function=None)
```

Provides a service instance for dependency injection.

- **Parameters**: - **service_class** (*type**[**AsyncServiceT_co**|**SyncServiceT_co**]*) – The service class to provide.
- **key** (*Optional**[**str**]*) – Optional key for the service.
- **statement** (*Optional**[**Select**[**tuple**[*[*ModelT*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.ModelT)*]**]**]*) – Optional SQLAlchemy statement.
- **error_messages** (*Optional**[**Union**[*[*ErrorMessages*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.ErrorMessages)*,*[*EmptyType*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dataclass.EmptyType)*]**]*) – Optional error messages.
- **load** (*Optional**[*[*LoadSpec*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.LoadSpec)*]*) – Optional load specification.
- **execution_options** (*Optional**[**dict**[**str**,**Any**]**]*) – Optional execution options.
- **uniquify** (*bool**|**None*) – Optional flag to uniquify the service.
- **count_with_window_function** (*bool**|**None*) – Optional flag to use window function for counting.
- **Returns**: A callable that returns an async generator for async services or a generator for sync services.
- **Return type**: *Callable*[…, *Union*[*AsyncGenerator*[AsyncServiceT_co, *None*], *Generator*[SyncServiceT_co, *None*, *None*]]]

##### `provide_filters`

```python
static provide_filters(config, /, dep_defaults=None)
```

Provides filters for dependency injection.

- **Parameters**: - **config** ([*FilterConfig*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/utils.html#advanced_alchemy.utils.dependencies.FilterConfig)) – The filters to provide.
- **dep_defaults** (*Optional**[*[*DependencyDefaults*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/fastapi/index.html#advanced_alchemy.extensions.fastapi.providers.DependencyDefaults)*]*) – Optional key for the filters.
- **Returns**: A callable that returns an async generator for async filters or a generator for sync filters.
- **Return type**: *Callable*[…, [*list*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/repository.html#advanced_alchemy.repository.SQLAlchemyAsyncRepository.list)[[*FilterTypes*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.FilterTypes)]]

## Dependency Providers

### `advanced_alchemy.extensions.fastapi.providers.provide_service`

```python
advanced_alchemy.extensions.fastapi.providers.provide_service(service_class, /, extension, key=None, statement=None, error_messages=Empty, load=None, execution_options=None, uniquify=None, count_with_window_function=None)[source]
```

Create a dependency provider for a service.

This function creates a generator-based dependency that manages
the service lifecycle. The generator owns the session lifecycle
and handles commit/rollback/close operations to ensure proper
connection pool management (especially important for asyncpg).

- **Returns**: A dependency provider for the service.
- **Return type**: *Callable*[[…], *AsyncGenerator*[*AsyncServiceT_co*, *None*] | *Generator*[*SyncServiceT_co*, *None*, *None*]]

### `advanced_alchemy.extensions.fastapi.providers.provide_filters`

| [*OnBeforeAfter*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.OnBeforeAfter) | [*BooleanFilter*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/filters.html#advanced_alchemy.filters.BooleanFilter) | # Starlette

API Reference for the `Starlette` extensions module.

## Extension & Middleware

### `advanced_alchemy.extensions.starlette.AdvancedAlchemy`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.extensions.starlette.AdvancedAlchemy(config, app=None)
```

Bases: `object`

AdvancedAlchemy integration for Starlette applications.

This class manages SQLAlchemy sessions and engine lifecycle within a Starlette application.
It provides middleware for handling transactions based on commit strategies.

- **Parameters**: - **config** ([*SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/starlette/index.html#advanced_alchemy.extensions.starlette.SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig)*|*[*SQLAlchemySyncConfig*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/starlette/index.html#advanced_alchemy.extensions.starlette.SQLAlchemySyncConfig)*|**Sequence**[*[*SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/starlette/index.html#advanced_alchemy.extensions.starlette.SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig)*|*[*SQLAlchemySyncConfig*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/starlette/index.html#advanced_alchemy.extensions.starlette.SQLAlchemySyncConfig)*]*) – The SQLAlchemy configuration.
- **app** (*Starlette**|**None*) – The Starlette application instance. Defaults to `None`.

##### `config`

```python
property config: Sequence[SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig | SQLAlchemySyncConfig]
```

Current Advanced Alchemy configuration.

##### `init_app`

```python
init_app(app)
```

Initializes the Starlette application with SQLAlchemy engine and sessionmaker.

Sets up middleware and shutdown handlers for managing the database engine.

- **Parameters**: **app** (*Starlette*) – The Starlette application instance.
- **Raises**: [**ImproperConfigurationError**](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.ImproperConfigurationError) – If the application is not initialized.

##### `lifespan`

```python
lifespan(app)
```

Context manager for lifespan events.

- **Parameters**: **app** (*Starlette*) – The starlette application.
- **Yields**: None
- **Return type**: *AsyncGenerator*[*Any*, *None*]

##### `app`

```python
property app: Starlette
```

Returns the Starlette application instance.

- **Raises**: [**ImproperConfigurationError**](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.ImproperConfigurationError) – If the application is not initialized.
- **Returns**: The Starlette application instance.

##### `on_startup`

```python
async on_startup()
```

Initializes the database.

##### `on_shutdown`

```python
async on_shutdown()
```

Handles the shutdown event by disposing of the SQLAlchemy engine.

Ensures that all connections are properly closed during application shutdown.

##### `map_configs`

```python
map_configs()
```

Maps the configs to the session bind keys.

- **Returns**: A dictionary of config bind keys to configs.
- **Return type**: *dict*[*str*, [*SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/starlette/index.html#advanced_alchemy.extensions.starlette.SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig) | [*SQLAlchemySyncConfig*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/starlette/index.html#advanced_alchemy.extensions.starlette.SQLAlchemySyncConfig)]

##### `get_config`

```python
get_config(key=None)
```

Get the config for the given key.

- **Parameters**: **key** (*str**|**None*) – The key to get the config for.
- **Raises**: [**ImproperConfigurationError**](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/exceptions.html#advanced_alchemy.exceptions.ImproperConfigurationError) – If the config is not found.
- **Returns**: The config for the given key.
- **Return type**: [*SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/starlette/index.html#advanced_alchemy.extensions.starlette.SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig) | [*SQLAlchemySyncConfig*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/starlette/index.html#advanced_alchemy.extensions.starlette.SQLAlchemySyncConfig)

- **Return type**: [*SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig*](https://docs.advanced-alchemy.litestar.dev/latest/reference/extensions/starlette/index.html#advanced_alchemy.extensions.starlette.SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig)

##### `get_sync_config`

```python
get_sync_config(key=None)
```

### `advanced_alchemy.extensions.starlette.config.SessionMiddleware`

```python
class advanced_alchemy.extensions.starlette.config.SessionMiddleware(app, config)[source]
```

Bases: `object`

Pure ASGI middleware for database session lifecycle management.

Unlike BaseHTTPMiddleware, this intercepts the `send` callable directly to capture
the response status code at the moment it is sent. This ensures `response_status`
is available on `request.state` before generator dependency cleanup runs, and avoids
known Starlette issues with BaseHTTPMiddleware and generator dependencies.

## Configuration

Get a session maker. If none exists yet, create one.

##### `session_handler`

```python
async session_handler(session, request, response)
```

Handles the session after a request is processed.

Applies the commit strategy and ensures the session is closed.

- **Parameters**: - **session** (*AsyncSession*) – The database session.
- **request** (*Request*) – The incoming HTTP request.
- **response** (*Response*) – The outgoing HTTP response.

##### `middleware_dispatch`

```python
async middleware_dispatch(request, call_next)
```

Middleware dispatch function to handle requests and responses.

Processes the request, invokes the next middleware or route handler, and
applies the session handler after the response is generated.

For generator-managed sessions (e.g., from provide_service()), the middleware
stores the response status but skips cleanup, allowing the generator to handle
commit/rollback/close operations properly.

- **Parameters**: - **request** (*Request*) – The incoming HTTP request.
- **call_next** (*RequestResponseEndpoint*) – The next middleware or route handler.
- **Returns**: The HTTP response.
- **Return type**: Response

##### `close_engine`

```python
async close_engine()
```

Close the engine.

##### `on_shutdown`

```python
async on_shutdown()
```

Handles the shutdown event by disposing of the SQLAlchemy engine.

Ensures that all connections are properly closed during application shutdown.

- **Return type**: *Any*

```python
json_serializer()
```

For dialects that support the JSON datatype, this is a Python callable that will render a given object as JSON.

- **Return type**: *str*

Get a session maker. If none exists yet, create one.

base-class implementation so configured session listeners for file
objects, timestamps, and cache invalidation are registered.

# utils

```

Drop all tables in the database.

- **Parameters**: - **engine** (*Union**[**AsyncEngine**,**Engine**]*) – The database engine.
- **version_table_name** (*str*) – The name of the version table.
